title.zh: 卷一百二十 列傳第七十: 郭子儀
title.raw: 卷一百二十 列傳第七十: 郭子儀 Volume 120 Biographies 70: Guo Ziyi

sentences.zh: 郭子儀子曜晞曖曙晤映晞子鋼曖子釗鏦釗子仲文族弟幼明子昕

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi's sons: Yao, Xi, Ai, Shu, Wu, Ying, and Xi; Ziyi's son Gang; Ai's son Zhao; Zhao's sons Cong and Zhongwen; clan younger brother Youming's son Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi's line included his sons Yao, Xi, Ai, Shu, Wu, and Ying, another son Xi, his son Gang, Ai's son Zhao (whose sons were Cong and Zhongwen), and his clansman Youming's son Xin.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀，華州鄭縣人。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi was a native of Zheng County in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi came from Zheng County in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父敬之，歷綏、渭、桂、壽、泗五州刺史，以子儀貴，贈太保，追封祁國公。

translations.literal: His father Jingzhi had served as prefect of the five prefectures of Sui, Wei, Gui, Shou, and Si; because of Ziyi's eminence, he was posthumously made Grand Mentor and enfeoffed as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guo Jingzhi had governed five prefectures—Sui, Wei, Gui, Shou, and Si—and when Ziyi rose to greatness, the court posthumously honored him as Grand Mentor and created him Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 子儀長六尺余，體貌秀傑，始以武舉高等補左衛長史，累歷諸軍使。

translations.literal: Ziyi stood over six chi in height, with a handsome and outstanding physique; he first entered service as Left Guard chief secretary after placing high in the military examination, and successively held various army commissioner posts.
translations.idiomatic: More than six feet tall and striking in bearing, Ziyi first joined the bureaucracy as chief secretary of the Left Guard after ranking high in the military exams, then served in a series of frontier army commands.

sentences.zh: 天寶八載，於木剌山置橫塞軍及安北都護府，命子儀領其使，拜左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao, the Hengsai Army and the Anbei Protectorate were established at Mula Mountain; Ziyi was appointed to command them and was made General-in-Chief of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 8 (749), the court founded the Hengsai Army and Anbei Protectorate at Mount Mula and put Ziyi in charge, promoting him to general-in-chief of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 十三載，移橫塞軍及安北都護府於永清柵北築城，仍改橫塞為天德軍，子儀為之使，兼九原太守、朔方節度右兵馬使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the Hengsai Army and Anbei Protectorate were moved to build a city north of Yongqing Stockade; Hengsai was renamed the Tiande Army, with Ziyi as its commissioner, concurrently prefect of Jiuyuan and right army commissioner of the Shuofang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 13 (754), the Hengsai forces and Anbei headquarters were relocated to a new fortress north of Yongqing; the unit became the Tiande Army under Ziyi, who also served as prefect of Jiuyuan and Shuofang's deputy army commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十四載，安祿山反。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, An Lushan rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 14 (755), An Lushan rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以子儀為衛尉卿，兼靈武郡太守，充朔方節度使，詔子儀以本軍東討。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Ziyi was made Minister of the Court of Imperial Studs and concurrently prefect of Lingwu Commandery, appointed military commissioner of Shuofang, and ordered to lead his army east to attack the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: That November, Ziyi became minister of the imperial stud and prefect of Lingwu, took command of Shuofang, and received orders to march east against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 遂舉兵出單於府，收靜邊軍，斬賊將周萬頃，傳首闕下。

translations.literal: He then raised troops from the Chanyu Protectorate, recovered the Jingbian Army, beheaded the rebel general Zhou Wanqing, and sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He mobilized from the Chanyu Protectorate, retook the Jingbian Army, executed the rebel commander Zhou Wanqing, and sent his head to the throne.

sentences.zh: 祿山遣大同軍使高秀巖寇河曲，子儀擊敗之，進收雲中馬邑，開東陘，以功加御史大夫。

translations.literal: Lushan sent the Datong Army commissioner Gao Xiuyan to raid the Yellow River bend; Ziyi defeated him, advanced to recover Yunzhong and Mayi, opened the eastern pass, and was promoted to Censor-in-Chief for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan dispatched Gao Xiuyan of the Datong Army to strike the river bend, Ziyi routed him, recaptured Yunzhong and Mayi, reopened the eastern pass, and earned promotion to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 十五載正月，賊將蔡希德陷常山郡，執顏杲卿，河北郡縣皆為賊守。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year, the rebel general Cai Xide captured Changshan Commandery and seized Yan Gaoqing; every commandery and county in Hebei fell to rebel garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 756, Cai Xide took Changshan, captured Yan Gaoqing, and left Hebei's counties in rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 二月，子儀與河東節度使李光弼率師下井陘，拔常山郡，破賊於九門，南攻趙郡，生擒賊四千，皆舍之，斬偽太守郭獻璆，獲兵仗數萬。

translations.literal: In the second month, Ziyi and Hedong military commissioner Li Guangbi led their forces down through Jingxing, retook Changshan, defeated the enemy at Jiumen, and pressed south into Zhao Commandery; they captured four thousand rebels and released them, beheaded the false prefect Guo Xianyao, and seized tens of thousands of weapons.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Ziyi and Li Guangbi descended Jingxing, recovered Changshan, smashed the rebels at Jiumen, and drove into Zhao Commandery—taking four thousand prisoners whom they freed, executing the puppet prefect Guo Xianyao, and capturing vast stores of arms.

sentences.zh: 師還常山，賊將史思明以數萬人踵其後，我行亦行，我止亦止。

translations.literal: The army returned to Changshan; the rebel general Shi Siming followed with tens of thousands—when we marched, he marched; when we halted, he halted.
translations.idiomatic: Marching back to Changshan, they found Shi Siming trailing with tens of thousands, matching their every halt and step.

sentences.zh: 子儀選驍騎五百更挑之，三日至行唐，賊疲乃退，我軍乘之，又敗於沙河。

translations.literal: Ziyi chose five hundred elite horsemen to harass them in relays; on the third day they reached Xingtang; when the rebels were exhausted they withdrew, and our army pressed them and defeated them again on the Sha River.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi sent five hundred picked cavalry to skirmish in rotation; by the third day at Xingtang the rebels were spent and fell back, and the Tang forces chased them to another victory on the Sha River.

sentences.zh: 祿山聞思明敗，乃以精兵益之。

translations.literal: When Lushan heard that Siming had been beaten, he sent elite troops to reinforce him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Siming's defeat, Lushan reinforced him with crack troops.

sentences.zh: 我軍至恆陽，賊亦隨至。

translations.literal: Our army reached Hengyang, and the rebels arrived as well.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang army reached Hengyang, the rebels closed in behind them.

sentences.zh: 子儀堅壁自固，賊來則守，賊去則追，晝揚其兵，夕襲其幕，賊人不及息。

translations.literal: Ziyi held fast behind strong walls; when the enemy came he defended, when they left he pursued—by day displaying his forces, by night raiding their camps, giving the rebels no rest.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi dug in: defending when attacked, pursuing when they withdrew, parading strength by day and striking camps at night until the enemy could not catch their breath.

sentences.zh: 數日，光弼議曰：「賊怠矣，可以戰。

translations.literal: After several days, Guangbi said in council, "The rebels are weary; we can fight."
translations.idiomatic: After several days Li Guangbi argued in council that the rebels had grown slack and the moment had come to give battle.

sentences.zh: 」六月，子儀、光弼率仆固懷恩、渾釋之、陳回光等陣於嘉山，賊將史思明、蔡希德、尹子奇等亦結陣而至，一戰敗之，斬馘四萬級，生擒五千人，獲馬五千匹，思明露髪跣足奔於博陵。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Ziyi and Guangbi, with Pugu Huai'en, Hun Jiezhi, Chen Huiguang, and others, formed battle lines at Jia Mountain; the rebel generals Shi Siming, Cai Xide, and Yin Ziqi likewise deployed—and in one clash were routed: forty thousand heads and captives, five thousand taken alive, five thousand horses seized; Siming fled to Boling bareheaded and barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Ziyi and Guangbi drew up at Jia Mountain with Pugu Huai'en, Hun Jiezhi, and Chen Huiguang against Siming, Cai Xide, and Yin Ziqi; one battle broke them—forty thousand slain or captured, five thousand prisoners, five thousand horses—and Siming fled barefoot and disheveled toward Boling.

sentences.zh: 於是河北十余郡皆斬賊守者以迎王師。

translations.literal: More than ten commanderies in Hebei then executed their rebel garrisons to welcome the imperial armies.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon more than ten Hebei prefectures killed their puppet officials and opened their gates to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 子儀將北圖范陽，軍聲大振。

translations.literal: Ziyi prepared to march north against Fanyang, and the army's reputation surged.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi turned toward Fanyang in the north, and the campaign's momentum swelled.

sentences.zh: 是月，哥舒翰為賊所敗，潼關不守，玄宗幸蜀，肅宗幸靈武，子儀副使杜鴻漸為朔方留後，奏迎車駕。

translations.literal: That month, Geshu Han was defeated by the rebels and Tong Pass fell; Emperor Xuanzong fled to Shu, Emperor Suzong to Lingwu; Ziyi's deputy Du Hongjian, left as Shuofang regent, memorialized to welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Geshu Han's defeat lost Tong Pass; Xuanzong fled to Shu and Suzong to Lingwu, while Du Hongjian, Ziyi's deputy left in charge of Shuofang, urged the court to welcome the new emperor.

sentences.zh: 七月，肅宗即位，以賊據兩京，方謀收復，詔子儀班師。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Suzong took the throne; with the rebels holding both capitals, the court plotted recovery and ordered Ziyi to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Suzong was enthroned; with Chang'an and Luoyang in enemy hands, he ordered Ziyi to pull his army back for the reconquest.

sentences.zh: 八月，子儀與李光弼率步騎五萬至自河北。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Ziyi and Li Guangbi brought fifty thousand infantry and cavalry from Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Ziyi and Li Guangbi arrived from Hebei with fifty thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷初立，兵眾寡弱，雖得牧馬，軍容缺然。

translations.literal: The dynasty was newly established, its forces few and weak; though pasture horses were available, military equipment was still lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The fledgling court had thin ranks; even with remounts at hand, the army still lacked proper kit.

sentences.zh: 及子儀、光弼全師赴行在，軍聲遂振，興復之勢，民有望焉。

translations.literal: When Ziyi and Guangbi brought their full strength to the emperor's camp, the army's prestige revived and the people dared hope for restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ziyi and Guangbi marched their intact armies to the imperial headquarters, morale revived and common people began to believe restoration possible.

sentences.zh: 詔以子儀為兵部尚書、同中書門下平章事，依前靈州大都督府長史、朔方軍節度使。

translations.literal: An edict made Ziyi Minister of War and co–Grand Councilor, retaining his posts as chief administrator of the Lingzhou metropolitan prefecture and military commissioner of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: The throne appointed Ziyi minister of war and grand councilor, while he kept his posts at Lingzhou and as Shuofang commissioner.

sentences.zh: 肅宗大閱六軍，南趨關輔，至彭原郡，宰相房琯請兵萬人，自為統帥以討賊，帝素重琯，許之。

translations.literal: Suzong reviewed the Six Armies and marched south toward the passes; at Pengyuan Commandery, chief councilor Fang Guan requested ten thousand men to lead personally against the rebels, and the emperor, who greatly esteemed Fang, consented.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong inspected the Six Armies and marched toward Guanzhong; at Pengyuan, Fang Guan asked for ten thousand troops to command himself, and the emperor, who trusted him deeply, agreed.

sentences.zh: 兵及陳濤，為賊所敗，喪師殆盡。

translations.literal: At Chen Tao the army was routed by the rebels and nearly annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: At Chen Tao, Fang Guan's force was smashed and almost wiped out.

sentences.zh: 方事討除，而軍半殪，唯倚朔方軍為根本。

translations.literal: Just as the campaign to destroy the rebels was underway, half the army was lost, and only the Shuofang army remained as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: With the great offensive barely begun, half the imperial force was gone, leaving Shuofang as the sole pillar.

sentences.zh: 十一月，賊將阿史那從禮以同羅、仆骨五千騎出塞，誘河曲九府、六胡州部落數萬，欲迫行在。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the rebel general Ashina Congli led five thousand Tongluo and Pugu horsemen out of the frontier and incited several tens of thousands from the nine prefectures and six Hu prefectures of the river bend to press the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Ashina Congli led five thousand Tongluo and Pugu cavalry from beyond the passes and stirred tens of thousands from the river-bend settlements to threaten the emperor's position.

sentences.zh: 子儀與回紇首領葛邏支往擊敗之，斬獲數萬，河曲平定。

translations.literal: Ziyi and the Uyghur chieftain Geluozhi went to attack and defeated them, killing and capturing tens of thousands, and the river bend was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi marched with the Uyghur leader Geluozhi, crushed the coalition, and took tens of thousands of heads and captives, pacifying the bend.

sentences.zh: 賊將崔乾祐守潼關。

translations.literal: The rebel general Cui Qianyou held Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Cui Qianyou guarded Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，子儀大破賊於潼關，崔乾祐退保蒲津。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, Ziyi won a great victory at Tong Pass and Cui Qianyou withdrew to defend Pujin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 757, Ziyi broke the rebels at Tong Pass, forcing Cui Qianyou back to Pujin.

sentences.zh: 時永樂尉趙復、河東司戶韓旻、司士徐炅、宗子李藏鋒等，陷賊在蒲州，四人密謀俟王師至，則為內應。

translations.literal: At that time the Yongle district defender Zhao Fu, Hedong registrar Han Min, legal officer Xu Jiong, and imperial clansman Li Cangfeng, trapped in Puzhou while it was held by rebels, secretly plotted to open the gates when the imperial army arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zhao Fu, Han Min, Xu Jiong, and Li Cangfeng, caught inside rebel-held Puzhou, plotted a rising when Tang troops appeared.

sentences.zh: 及子儀攻蒲州，趙復等斬賊守陴者，開門納子儀。

translations.literal: When Ziyi attacked Puzhou, Zhao Fu and the others cut down the rebel gate guards and opened the city to Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: As Ziyi besieged Puzhou, they killed the wall guards and admitted his army.

sentences.zh: 乾祐與麾下數千人北走安邑，安邑百姓偽降，乾祐兵入將半，下懸門擊之，乾祐未入，遂得脫身東走。

translations.literal: Qianyou fled north toward Anyi with several thousand followers; the people of Anyi feigned surrender, and when half his force had entered they dropped the portcullis on them—Qianyou had not yet entered and escaped eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyou fled north to Anyi with a few thousand men; the townspeople feigned submission, then dropped the gate on his column before he could enter, and he slipped away east.

sentences.zh: 子儀遂收陜郡永豐倉。

translations.literal: Ziyi then recovered the Yongfeng granary in Shaan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi next seized the Yongfeng granary in Shaan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 自是潼、陜之間無復寇鈔。

translations.literal: From then on there was no more raiding between Tong and Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: After that, banditry between Tong and Shaan ceased.

sentences.zh: 是月，安祿山死，朝廷欲圖大舉，詔子儀還鳳翔。

translations.literal: That month, An Lushan died; the court planned a major offensive and ordered Ziyi back to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: That month An Lushan died; the court prepared a grand campaign and recalled Ziyi to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 四月，進位司空，充關內、河東副元帥。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, he was promoted to Minister of Works and made deputy commander-in-chief of Guannei and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he became minister of works and deputy supreme commander for Guannei and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔子儀帥師趨京城。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, an edict ordered Ziyi to lead the army toward the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the emperor ordered him to advance on Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 師於潏水之西，與賊將安太清、安守忠戰，王師不利，其眾大潰，盡委兵仗於清渠之上。

translations.literal: The army fought west of the Wei River against the rebel generals An Taiqing and An Shouzhong; the imperial force fared badly and broke, abandoning weapons and gear along the Qing Canal.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Wei River they clashed with An Taiqing and An Shouzhong, suffered a disastrous rout, and littered the Qing Canal with discarded arms.

sentences.zh: 子儀收合余眾，保武功，詣闕請罪，乞降官資，乃降為左僕射，余如故。

translations.literal: Ziyi gathered the remnants, held Wugong, came to court to confess fault, and begged to be demoted—he was reduced to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs while keeping his other posts.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi regrouped at Wugong, presented himself to accept blame, and asked for demotion; he was lowered to left vice director of the Secretariat while retaining his other titles.

sentences.zh: 九月，從元帥廣平王率蕃漢之師十五萬進收長安。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he followed the commander-in-chief the Prince of Guangping, leading a mixed force of fifteen thousand Tang and non-Han troops to recover Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he served under the Prince of Guangping, leading one hundred fifty thousand Tang and allied troops to retake Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 回紇遣葉護太子領四千騎助國討賊，子儀與葉護宴狎修好，相與誓平國難，相得甚好。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs sent Prince Yehu with four thousand horsemen to aid the dynasty; Ziyi feasted and bonded with Yehu, swore together to end the national crisis, and they got on excellently.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs sent Prince Yehu with four thousand riders; Ziyi banqueted with him, pledged to end the crisis together, and won his warm trust.

sentences.zh: 子儀奉元帥為中軍，與賊將安守忠、李歸仁戰於京西香積寺之北，王師結陣橫亙三十里，賊眾十萬陳於北。

translations.literal: Ziyi placed the commander-in-chief at the center and fought the rebel generals An Shouzhong and Li Guiren north of Xiangji Temple west of the capital; the imperial line stretched thirty li while one hundred thousand rebels stood to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi anchored the prince at the center against An Shouzhong and Li Guiren north of Xiangji Temple; the Tang front spanned thirty li facing one hundred thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 歸仁先薄我軍，我軍亂，李嗣業奮命馳突，擒賊十余騎乃定。

translations.literal: Guiren struck first and threw the line into disorder; Li Siye charged desperately, seized more than ten rebel riders, and steadied the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Guiren hit the front, the line buckled until Li Siye charged, grabbed a dozen rebel horsemen, and held the formation.

sentences.zh: 回紇以奇兵出賊陣之後夾攻之，賊軍大潰，自午至酉，斬首六萬級。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs sent a flanking force behind the rebel array to attack from both sides; the rebel army collapsed; from noon to dusk sixty thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Uyghur horsemen swept behind the rebel line in a pincer; the enemy army collapsed, and from noon to evening sixty thousand were slain.

sentences.zh: 賊將張通儒守長安，聞歸仁等敗，是夜奔陜郡。

translations.literal: The rebel general Zhang Tongru, holding Chang'an, heard of Guiren's defeat and fled that night to Shaan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tongru, garrison commander in Chang'an, fled overnight to Shaan when he heard of Guiren's rout.

sentences.zh: 翌日，廣平王入京師，老幼百萬，夾道歡叫，涕泣而言曰：「不圖今日復見官軍。

translations.literal: The next day the Prince of Guangping entered the capital; a million old and young lined the roads, weeping and shouting, "We never thought to see imperial troops again today."
translations.idiomatic: The next day the prince entered the city; a million citizens lined the streets in tears, crying that they never expected to see imperial soldiers again.

sentences.zh: 」廣平王休士三日，率師東趨。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangping rested the troops three days, then marched east.
translations.idiomatic: After three days' rest, the prince led the army eastward.

sentences.zh: 肅宗在鳳翔聞捷，群臣稱賀，帝以宗廟被焚，悲咽不自勝，臣僚無不感泣。

translations.literal: Suzong, at Fengxiang, heard the victory; the court congratulated him, but the emperor, remembering the burned ancestral temples, sobbed uncontrollably, and every official wept.
translations.idiomatic: At Fengxiang, Suzong rejoiced at the news, then broke down remembering the burned ancestral shrines, and the whole court wept with him.

sentences.zh: 十月，安慶緒遣嚴莊悉其眾十萬來赴陜州，與張通儒同抗官軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, An Qingxu sent Yan Zhuang with one hundred thousand men to reinforce Shaanzhou, joining Zhang Tongru to resist the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, An Qingxu dispatched Yan Zhuang with one hundred thousand men to Shaanzhou alongside Zhang Tongru to block the Tang.

sentences.zh: 賊聞官軍至，悉其眾屯於陜西，負山為陣。

translations.literal: Hearing the imperial army approach, the rebels massed west of Shaan and leaned on the mountains for their formation.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels gathered west of Shaan, anchoring their battle line on the hills.

sentences.zh: 子儀以大軍擊其前，回紇登山乘其背，遇賊潛師於山中，與鬥過期，大軍稍卻。

translations.literal: Ziyi struck from the front while the Uyghurs climbed the heights to hit their rear; hidden rebel troops in the hills delayed the clash, and the main force fell back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi attacked head-on as Uyghurs scaled the heights; rebel ambushes in the hills delayed the engagement and the main Tang line edged back.

sentences.zh: 賊分兵三千人，絕我歸路，眾心大搖，子儀麾回紇令進，盡殺之。

translations.literal: The rebels sent three thousand men to cut off the retreat; panic spread until Ziyi ordered the Uyghurs forward and they slaughtered the blocking force.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels sent three thousand men to sever the retreat; morale wavered until Ziyi drove the Uyghurs forward and they wiped out the detachment.

sentences.zh: 師馳至其後，於黃埃中發十余箭，賊驚顧曰：「回紇來！

translations.literal: The Uyghurs galloped to the enemy rear and loosed more than ten arrows from the yellow dust; the rebels looked back in alarm and cried, "The Uyghurs are coming!"
translations.idiomatic: Uyghur riders raced to the rear and fired a volley from the dust; the enemy looked back in terror shouting that the Uyghurs had come.

sentences.zh: 」即時大敗，僵屍遍山澤。

translations.literal: At once they were utterly defeated, corpses covering hills and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Instantly they were routed, and the slopes and marshes were heaped with dead.

sentences.zh: 嚴莊、張通儒走歸洛陽，遂與安慶緒渡河保相州。

translations.literal: Yan Zhuang and Zhang Tongru fled to Luoyang, then crossed the river with An Qingxu to hold Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhuang and Zhang Tongru ran to Luoyang, then crossed the Yellow River with An Qingxu to defend Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子儀奉廣平王入東都，陳兵於天津橋南，士庶歡呼於路。

translations.literal: Ziyi escorted the Prince of Guangping into the Eastern Capital and paraded troops south of the Tianjin Bridge while citizens cheered along the route.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi brought the prince into Luoyang and drew up troops south of the Tianjin Bridge as the city shouted its joy.

sentences.zh: 偽侍中陳希烈、偽中書令張垍等三百余人素服請罪，王慰撫遣之。

translations.literal: The false chief councilor Chen Xilie, false grand councilor Zhang Ao, and more than three hundred others came in white robes to beg forgiveness; the prince comforted them and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Over three hundred puppet officials, including Chen Xilie and Zhang Ao, surrendered in mourning dress; the prince reassured and released them.

sentences.zh: 是時，河東、河西、河南賊所盜郡邑皆平，以功加司徒，封代國公，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: By then rebel-held counties in Hedong, Hexi, and Henan had been recovered; for his merit he was made Minister of Education, created Duke of Dai, with an estate of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: With rebel territories in Hedong, Hexi, and Henan restored, he was made minister of education, created Duke of Dai, and granted a thousand-household fief.

sentences.zh: 尋入朝，天子遣兵仗戎容迎於灞上，肅宗勞之曰：「雖吾之家國，實由卿再造。

translations.literal: Soon he attended court; the Son of Heaven sent an armed escort to welcome him at Bashang; Suzong praised him, saying, "Though it is my house and state, in truth you remade it."
translations.idiomatic: He soon came to court; the emperor sent a military escort to Bashang, where Suzong told him, "This realm is mine, but you remade it."

sentences.zh: 」子儀頓首感謝。

translations.literal: Ziyi bowed his head in gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 十二月，還東都，命子儀經營北討。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, he returned to the Eastern Capital and was ordered to plan the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he went back to Luoyang to organize the northern offensive.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年七月，破賊河上，擒偽將安守忠以獻，遂朝京師，敕百僚班迎於長樂驛，帝御望春樓待之，進位中書令。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Qianyuan, he broke the rebels on the river, captured the false general An Shouzhong and presented him, then came to the capital; the emperor ordered the bureaucracy to welcome him at Changle Post and received him at Wangchun Tower, promoting him to Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianyuan 1, seventh month, he defeated the rebels on the river, sent up An Shouzhong as a captive, and was welcomed at Changle Post and received at Wangchun Tower, rising to grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 九月，奉詔大舉，子儀與河東節度使李光弼、關內節度使王思禮、北庭行營節度李嗣業、襄鄧節度使魯炅、荊南節度季廣琛、河南節度使崔光遠、滑濮節度許叔冀、平盧兵馬使董秦等九節度之師討安慶緒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, by edict a great campaign was launched: Ziyi with Hedong commissioner Li Guangbi, Guannei commissioner Wang Sili, Beiting field commissioner Li Siye, Xiang-Deng commissioner Lu Jiong, Jingnan commissioner Ji Guangchen, Henan commissioner Cui Guangyuan, Hua-Pu commissioner Xu Shuji, and Pinglu army commissioner Dong Qin—nine circuits— marched against An Qingxu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month nine circuits—under Ziyi, Li Guangbi, Wang Sili, Li Siye, Lu Jiong, Ji Guangchen, Cui Guangyuan, Xu Shuji, and Dong Qin—were ordered to destroy An Qingxu.

sentences.zh: 帝以子儀、光弼俱是元勛，難相統屬，故不立元帥。

translations.literal: Because both Ziyi and Guangbi were founding heroes, the emperor found it hard to subordinate one to the other, so no supreme commander was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Since both Ziyi and Guangbi were paramount heroes, the throne appointed no single supreme commander over them.

sentences.zh: 唯以中官魚朝恩為觀軍容宣慰使。

translations.literal: Only the eunuch Yu Chao'en was made army-inspecting envoy and commissioner of consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Only the eunuch Yu Chao'en was named army-inspecting envoy and imperial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十月，子儀自杏園渡河，圍衛州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Ziyi crossed the Yellow River from Xingyuan and besieged Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Ziyi crossed from Xingyuan and invested Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 安慶緒與其驍將安雄俊、崔乾祐、薛嵩、田承嗣悉其眾來援，分為三軍。

translations.literal: An Qingxu came with his fierce generals An Xiongjun, Cui Qianyou, Xue Song, and Tian Chengsi at full strength in three armies to relieve the city.
translations.idiomatic: An Qingxu marched with An Xiongjun, Cui Qianyou, Xue Song, and Tian Chengsi in three armies to break the siege.

sentences.zh: 子儀陣以待之，預選射者三千人伏於壁內，誡之曰：「俟吾小卻，賊必爭進，則登城鼓噪，弓弩齊發以迫之。

translations.literal: Ziyi formed his line to receive them, preselected three thousand archers hidden within the walls, and warned them, "When I feign a slight retreat and the rebels rush forward, mount the walls, shout, and let fly together to drive them back."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi drew up to meet them, hid three thousand archers on the walls, and instructed them to raise a clamor and volley when he pretended to give ground.

sentences.zh: 」既戰，子儀偽遁，賊果乘之，及壘門，遽聞鼓噪，俄而弓弩齊發，矢註如雨，賊徒震駭，子儀整眾追之，賊眾大敗。

translations.literal: When battle joined, Ziyi feigned flight; the rebels pursued as expected; at the gate came sudden drums and a rain of arrows; the enemy panicked; Ziyi reformed and chased them to a great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi faked a retreat; the rebels chased to the ramparts; drums and arrows burst forth; the rebels shattered, and Ziyi reformed and routed them.

sentences.zh: 是役也，獲偽鄭王安慶和以獻，遂收衛州。

translations.literal: In this battle the false Prince of Zheng An Qinghe was captured and presented; Weizhou was taken.
translations.idiomatic: They captured the puppet Prince of Zheng, An Qinghe, and took Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 進軍趨鄴，與賊再戰於愁思岡，賊軍又敗，乃連營圍之。

translations.literal: The army advanced toward Ye and fought the rebels again at Chousi Ridge; the rebels were beaten again and were closely besieged.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing toward Ye, they beat the rebels again at Chousi Ridge and tightened the siege.

sentences.zh: 慶緒遣薛嵩以所乘馬十匹求救於史思明，且言禪代。

translations.literal: Qingxu sent Xue Song with ten of his own horses to beg Shi Siming for help and spoke of abdicating the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu sent Xue Song with ten of his own horses to plead with Shi Siming and offered to yield the throne.

sentences.zh: 十二月，思明遣將李歸仁率眾赴之，營於滏陽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Siming sent Li Guiren to encamp at Fuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Siming dispatched Li Guiren to camp at Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，史思明自率范陽精卒復陷魏州，乃偽稱燕王。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, Shi Siming personally led elite Fanyang troops, retook Weizhou, and falsely declared himself King of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, first month, Siming led Fanyang veterans, recaptured Weizhou, and proclaimed himself King of Yan.

sentences.zh: 王師雖眾，軍無統帥，進退無所承稟，自冬徂春，竟未破賊，但引漳水以灌其城，城中食盡，易子而食。

translations.literal: Though the imperial army was numerous, it had no unified commander; advance and retreat had no authority to follow; from winter to spring the city was never taken—only the Zhang River was diverted to flood it until food inside was gone and people exchanged children to eat.
translations.idiomatic: The allied host was huge but leaderless; through winter into spring Ye never fell—only the Zhang was dammed to starve the city until families traded children for food.

sentences.zh: 二月，思明率眾自魏州來。

translations.literal: In the second month, Siming led his army from Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Siming marched from Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 李光弼、王思禮、許叔冀、魯炅前軍遇賊於鄴南，與之接戰，夷傷相半，魯炅中流矢。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi, Wang Sili, Xu Shuji, and Lu Jiong's vanguard met the rebels south of Ye and fought; casualties were about even, and Lu Jiong was struck by a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi, Wang Sili, Xu Shuji, and Lu Jiong's vanguard clashed south of Ye with roughly equal losses; Lu Jiong took an arrow.

sentences.zh: 子儀為後陣，未及合戰，大風遽起，吹沙拔木，天地晦暝，跬步不辯物色。

translations.literal: Ziyi held the rear and had not yet joined battle when a sudden gale rose, blowing sand and uprooting trees; heaven and earth darkened, and one could not see a step ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi was in the rear when a sandstorm uprooted trees and blacked out the field so men could not see a pace ahead.

sentences.zh: 我師潰而南，賊軍潰而北，委棄兵仗輜重，累積於路。

translations.literal: Our army broke south while the rebel army broke north, abandoning weapons and baggage piled along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang line collapsed southward and the rebel line northward, leaving the roads littered with arms and wagons.

sentences.zh: 諸軍各還本鎮。

translations.literal: Each army returned to its home circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Each contingent withdrew to its own territory.

sentences.zh: 子儀以朔方軍保河陽，斷浮橋，有詔令留守東都。

translations.literal: Ziyi held Heyang with the Shuofang army, cut the pontoon bridge, and was ordered to remain at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi held Heyang with Shuofang troops, severed the floating bridge, and was ordered to stay in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 三月，以子儀為東都畿、山南東道、河南諸道行營元帥。

translations.literal: In the third month, Ziyi was made commander-in-chief of the Eastern Capital metropolitan, Shannan East, and Henan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he became field marshal over the Eastern Capital, Shannan East, and Henan circuits.

sentences.zh: 中官魚朝恩素害子儀之功，因其不振，媒孽之，尋召還京師。

translations.literal: The eunuch Yu Chao'en had long resented Ziyi's achievements; seizing on the setback, he slandered him, and soon Ziyi was recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chao'en, jealous of Ziyi's fame, used the defeat to slander him, and Ziyi was soon recalled.

sentences.zh: 天子以趙王系為天下兵馬元帥，李光弼副之，委以陜東軍事，代子儀之任。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven made the Prince of Zhao supreme commander of all armies, with Li Guangbi as deputy, entrusting him with Shaan-dong military affairs in place of Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made the Prince of Zhao supreme commander with Li Guangbi as deputy, replacing Ziyi in the east.

sentences.zh: 子儀雖失兵柄，乃思王室，以禍難未平，不遑寢息。

translations.literal: Though Ziyi lost command of troops, he still thought of the royal house; with calamity not yet ended, he had no leisure to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of command, he still burned for the dynasty and could not rest while rebellion lingered.

sentences.zh: 俄而史思明再陷河洛，朝廷旰食，復慮蕃寇逼迫京畿，三年正月，授子儀邠寧、鄜坊兩鎮節度使，仍留京師。

translations.literal: Before long Shi Siming again seized the Yellow River and Luoyang; the court ate late meals in anxiety, fearing non-Han raiders would threaten the capital; in the third year, first month, Ziyi was made military commissioner of Binning and Fufang but remained at court.
translations.idiomatic: When Siming retook the heartland, the court ate in haste, fearing barbarian raids on Chang'an; in the third year's first month Ziyi was given Binning and Fufang but kept in the capital.

sentences.zh: 言事者以子儀有社稷大功，今殘孽未除，不宜置之散地，肅宗深然之。

translations.literal: Memorialists argued that Ziyi's service to the altars of soil and grain was too great and that with remnants still active he should not be left idle; Suzong deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials urged that a man of Ziyi's stature should not sit idle while rebels remained; Suzong strongly concurred.

sentences.zh: 上元元年九月，以子儀為諸道兵馬都統，管崇嗣副之，令率英武、威遠等禁軍及河西、河東諸鎮之師，取邠寧、朔方、大同、橫野，徑抵范陽。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Shangyuan, Ziyi was made overall commander of all circuits' armies, with Guan Chongsi as deputy, ordered to lead the Yingwu, Weiyuan, and other palace guards plus Hexi and Hedong contingents to take Binning, Shuofang, Datong, and Hengye and strike straight at Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan 1, ninth month, he was named overall commander with Guan Chongsi as deputy to lead palace guards and western armies through Binning and Shuofang toward Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 詔下旬日，復為朝恩所間，事竟不行。

translations.literal: The edict was to take effect in ten days, but Yu Chao'en interfered again and the plan never went forward.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Yu Chao'en sabotaged the order and the campaign was canceled.

sentences.zh: 上元二年二月，李光弼兵敗於邙山，河陽失守，魚朝恩退保陜州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Shangyuan, Li Guangbi was defeated at Mount Mang, Heyang fell, and Yu Chao'en withdrew to Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Shangyuan 2, second month, Guangbi lost at Mount Mang, Heyang fell, and Yu Chao'en pulled back to Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，河中軍亂，殺其帥李國貞。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, the Hezhong army mutinied and killed its commander Li Guozhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, second month, troops at Hezhong murdered their commander Li Guozhen.

sentences.zh: 時太原節度鄧景山亦為部下所殺，恐其合從連賊，朝廷憂之。

translations.literal: At the same time Taiyuan commissioner Deng Jingshan was also killed by his subordinates; fearing they would join forces with rebels, the court was deeply alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiyuan commissioner Deng Jingshan was likewise murdered, the court feared a rebel alliance and grew alarmed.

sentences.zh: 後輩帥臣未能彈壓，勢不獲已，遂用子儀為朔方、河中、北庭、潞、儀、澤、沁等州節度行營兼興平、定國副元帥，充本管觀察處置使，進封汾陽郡王，出鎮絳州。

translations.literal: Junior commanders could not suppress the unrest; with no choice, Ziyi was made field commissioner of Shuofang, Hezhong, Beiting, Lu, Yi, Ze, Qin, and related circuits, deputy commander-in-chief of Xingping and Dingguo, observation and disposition commissioner of his jurisdiction, created Prince of Fenyang, and sent to govern from Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to restrain the mutinies, the throne turned to Ziyi as deputy supreme commander and commissioner over Shuofang, Hezhong, Beiting, and other circuits, created him Prince of Fenyang, and sent him to Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，子儀辭赴鎮，肅宗不豫，群臣莫有見者。

translations.literal: In the third month, Ziyi took leave to go to his post; Suzong was ill and no official had been received in audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Ziyi prepared to depart; Suzong was unwell and had seen no courtier.

sentences.zh: 子儀請曰：「老臣受命，將死於外，不見陛下，目不瞑矣。

translations.literal: Ziyi petitioned, saying, "This old subject has received orders and will die abroad; if I do not see Your Majesty, my eyes will not close."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi pleaded: "I have been ordered to serve until death in the provinces—if I do not see Your Majesty, I cannot die in peace."

sentences.zh: 」帝乃引至臥內，謂子儀曰：「河東之事，一以委卿。

translations.literal: The emperor then led him into the inner chamber and said to Ziyi, "The affairs of Hedong I entirely entrust to you."
translations.idiomatic: Suzong brought him to the bedside and said, "All matters in Hedong I leave entirely in your hands."

sentences.zh: 」子儀嗚咽流涕。

translations.literal: Ziyi sobbed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 賜禦馬、銀器、雜彩，別賜絹四萬疋、布五萬端以賞軍。

translations.literal: He was granted an imperial horse, silver vessels, and assorted silks; separately he was given forty thousand bolts of silk and fifty thousand lengths of cloth to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: The court bestowed an imperial horse, silverware, and colored silks, plus forty thousand bolts of silk and fifty thousand lengths of cloth to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 子儀至絳，擒其殺國貞賊首王元振數十人誅之。

translations.literal: When Ziyi reached Jiang, he captured several tens of the ringleaders who had killed Guozhen, including Wang Yuanzhen, and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangzhou he seized dozens of mutineers led by Wang Yuanzhen, who had murdered Guozhen, and put them to death.

sentences.zh: 太原辛雲京聞子儀誅元振，亦誅害景山者，由是河東諸鎮率皆奉法。

translations.literal: Xin Yunjing of Taiyuan, hearing that Ziyi had executed Yuanzhen, likewise executed Deng Jingshan's killers; thereafter the circuits of Hedong generally obeyed the law.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiyuan's Xin Yunjing heard of Yuanzhen's execution, he too punished Deng Jingshan's murderers, and Hedong's garrisons thereafter mostly kept discipline.

sentences.zh: 四月，代宗即位，內官程元振用事，自矜定策之功，忌嫉宿將，以子儀功高難制，巧行離間，請罷副元帥，加實封七百戶，充肅宗山陵使。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Emperor Daizong succeeded; the inner court official Cheng Yuanzhen held power, priding himself on his role in settling the succession, jealous of veteran generals; because Ziyi's merit was too great to control, he craftily sowed discord, asked to remove the deputy commander-in-chief title, added seven hundred actual fief households, and made him commissioner for Emperor Suzong's mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Daizong ascended; eunuch Cheng Yuanzhen, vaunting his role in the succession, envied old commanders and, finding Ziyi too powerful to manage, slandered him, stripped his deputy commander title, added seven hundred fief households, and made him overseer of Suzong's tomb.

sentences.zh: 子儀既謝恩，上表進肅宗所賜前後詔敕，因自陳訴曰：

translations.literal: After Ziyi had thanked for the grace, he memorialized presenting the edicts and orders Suzong had granted him before and after, and lodged a personal petition saying:
translations.idiomatic: After accepting the honors, Ziyi submitted the accumulated edicts Suzong had given him and filed a personal appeal:

sentences.zh: 臣德薄蟬翼，命輕鴻毛，累蒙國恩，猥廁朝列。

translations.literal: Your subject's virtue is thinner than a cicada's wing, his life lighter than a goose feather; yet I have repeatedly received the state's favor and unworthily stand in the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: My virtue is thinner than a cicada's wing and my life lighter than a goose down, yet the throne has heaped favor on me and placed me among ministers.

sentences.zh: 會天地震蕩，中原血戰，臣北自靈武，冊先皇帝，乃舉兵而南，大搜於岐陽。

translations.literal: When heaven and earth shook and the central plains ran with blood, your subject came north from Lingwu to invest the late emperor, then raised troops southward and mustered a great hunt at Qiyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm convulsed and the heartland ran with blood, I came from Lingwu to support the late emperor, then marched south and gathered forces at Qiyang.

sentences.zh: 先帝憂勤宗社，托臣以家國，俾副陛下掃兩京之妖昆。

translations.literal: The late emperor, anxious for the altars of state, entrusted house and realm to me, bidding me assist Your Majesty in sweeping the demonic brood from the two capitals.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor, laboring for the dynasty, entrusted me with house and realm to help Your Majesty cleanse the two capitals of rebels.

sentences.zh: 陛下雄圖丕斷，再造區宇，自後不以臣寡劣，委文武之二柄，外敷邦教，內調鼎飪，是以常許國家之死，實荷日月之明。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's heroic resolve renewed the realm; afterward, not deeming me weak and inferior, you entrusted both civil and military power— governing abroad and seasoning the cauldron within—so that I often pledged my life to the state and truly bore the brightness of sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's decisive vision restored the empire; despite my unworthiness you gave me both civil and military authority at home and abroad, and I pledged my life to the state under your radiant trust.

sentences.zh: 臣本愚淺，言多詆直，慮此招謗，上瀆冕旒。

translations.literal: Your subject is by nature shallow and blunt, and my words are often slanderously straight; fearing this invites calumny, I have offended the imperial crown.
translations.idiomatic: I am dull and blunt of speech, often giving offense; I feared slander had already stained your ear.

sentences.zh: 陛下居高聽卑，察臣不貳，皇天後土，察臣無私。

translations.literal: Your Majesty sits high and listens low, discerning my loyalty; heaven above and earth below witness my lack of selfishness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty listens from on high and sees my loyalty; heaven and earth know I am without private aim.

sentences.zh: 伏以器忌滿盈，日增兢惕，焉敢偷全，久妨賢路？

translations.literal: I reflect that vessels dread overflowing; daily I grow more cautious—how dare I steal wholeness and long block the path of the worthy?
translations.idiomatic: Vessels fear overfilling; each day I grow more wary—how could I cling to office and block better men?

sentences.zh: 自受恩塞下，制敵行間，東西十年，前後百戰。

translations.literal: Since receiving favor on the frontier, commanding against the enemy in the field, east and west for ten years, in battles before and behind a hundred times.
translations.idiomatic: Since the frontier honors, fighting east and west for ten years through a hundred battles,

sentences.zh: 天寒劍折，濺血沾衣；

translations.literal: In freezing cold swords broke and splashed blood stained our robes;
translations.idiomatic: in freezing cold blades snapped and blood spattered our coats;

sentences.zh: 野宿魂驚，飲冰傷骨。

translations.literal: sleeping in the wild souls trembled, drinking ice injured the bones.
translations.idiomatic: sleeping in the open we shook with fear, drinking melted ice we hurt to the bone.

sentences.zh: 跋涉難阻，出沒死生，所仗唯天，以至今日。

translations.literal: Through hardships hard to cross, appearing and vanishing between life and death, what I relied on was only heaven, down to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Through hardships and the brink of death I relied on heaven alone to reach this day.

sentences.zh: 陛下曲申惠獎，念及勤勞，貽臣詔書一千余首，聖旨微婉，慰諭綢繆，彰微臣一時之功，成子孫萬代之寶。

translations.literal: Your Majesty graciously extended rewards, mindful of my toil, bestowing on me more than a thousand edicts—imperial words subtle and warm, consolation intimate—glorifying your subject's momentary service and making a treasure for ten thousand generations of descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rewarded my labor with more than a thousand edicts—gracious, intimate words that ennoble my service and become my heirs' heirloom.

sentences.zh: 自靈武、河北、河南、彭原、鄜坊、河東、鳳翔、兩京、絳州，臣所經行，賜手詔敕書凡二十卷，昧死上進，庶煩聽覽。

translations.literal: From Lingwu, Hebei, Henan, Pengyuan, Fufang, Hedong, Fengxiang, the two capitals, and Jiangzhou—wherever I passed—the hand-edicts and orders granted me fill twenty scrolls in all; risking death I present them above, that Your Majesty may deign to review them.
translations.idiomatic: Hand-edicts from every campaign—from Lingwu to the two capitals and Jiangzhou—fill twenty scrolls, which I risk death to submit for your review.

sentences.zh: 詔答曰：「朕不德不明，俾大臣憂疑，朕之過也。

translations.literal: The edict replied: "I am lacking in virtue and unclear in judgment, causing great ministers worry and doubt—the fault is mine."
translations.idiomatic: The reply read: "My virtue is wanting and my judgment unclear; I have troubled my ministers—the fault is mine."

sentences.zh: 朕甚自愧，公勿以為慮。

translations.literal: I am deeply ashamed myself; do not let this weigh on you."
translations.idiomatic: I am deeply ashamed; do not brood on it."

sentences.zh: 」代宗以子儀頃同患難，收復兩京，禮之逾厚。

translations.literal: Daizong, because Ziyi had shared hardships and recovered the two capitals, treated him with ever greater courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong, remembering shared hardship and the recovery of the capitals, honored Ziyi ever more generously.

sentences.zh: 時史朝義尚據洛陽，元帥雍王率師進討，代宗欲以子儀副之，而魚朝恩、程元振亂政，殺裴茂、來瑱，子儀既為所間，其事遂寢，乃留京師。

translations.literal: At that time Shi Chaoyi still held Luoyang; the commander-in-chief the Prince of Yong led troops to attack; Daizong wished to make Ziyi his deputy, but Yu Chao'en and Cheng Yuanzhen's corrupt rule killed Pei Miao and Lai Tian; Ziyi was slandered by them and the plan was shelved, and he remained at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: While Shi Chaoyi held Luoyang and the Prince of Yong marched against him, Daizong wanted Ziyi as deputy, but Yu and Cheng's faction killed Pei Miao and Lai Tian and slandered Ziyi until the appointment died and he stayed in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 俄而梁崇義據襄陽叛，仆固懷恩阻兵於汾州，引回紇、吐蕃之眾入寇河西。

translations.literal: Soon Liang Chongyi rebelled at Xiangyang, Pugu Huai'en held out with troops at Fenzhou, and led Uyghur and Tibetan forces to raid Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liang Chongyi rebelled in Xiangyang, Pugu Huai'en mutinied at Fenzhou, and Uyghur and Tibetan armies raided Hexi.

sentences.zh: 明年十月，吐蕃陷涇州，虜刺史高暉，暉遂與蕃軍為鄉導，引賊深入京畿，掠奉天、武功，濟渭而南，緣山而東。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the following year, Tibet took Jingzhou and captured Prefect Gao Hui; Hui then guided the Tibetan army as a local guide, leading the enemy deep into the capital region, plundering Fengtian and Wugong, crossing the Wei southward and following the mountains east.
translations.idiomatic: Next tenth month Tibet took Jingzhou and captured Prefect Gao Hui, who then guided them deep toward the capital, looting Fengtian and Wugong, crossing the Wei and marching east along the hills.

sentences.zh: 渭北行營兵馬使呂日將逆戰於盩厔，自辰至酉，殺蕃軍數千，然其徒多殞。

translations.literal: The Weibei field army commissioner Lu Riji met them in battle at Zhouzhi from the chen hour to the you hour, killing several thousand Tibetans, but many of his men also fell.
translations.idiomatic: Weibei commissioner Lu Riji fought them at Zhouzhi from morning to evening, killing thousands of Tibetans at heavy cost.

sentences.zh: 賊將逼京師，君上計無所出，遽詔子儀為關內副元帥，出鎮咸陽。

translations.literal: As rebel troops pressed the capital and the sovereign had no plan, an urgent edict suddenly made Ziyi deputy commander-in-chief of Guannei and sent him to garrison Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: With the enemy nearing Chang'an and no plan at hand, the emperor suddenly named Ziyi deputy commander of Guannei and sent him to Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 子儀自相州不利，李光弼代掌兵柄，及征還朝廷，部曲散去。

translations.literal: Ziyi, since the setback at Xiangzhou, had Li Guangbi replace him in command; when recalled to court his followers dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiangzhou, Li Guangbi took his command; recalled to court, his retinue melted away.

sentences.zh: 及是承詔，部下唯二十騎，強取民家畜產以助軍。

translations.literal: When he now received the edict, his following was only twenty horsemen; he forcibly requisitioned livestock from households to support the army.
translations.idiomatic: On this new order he had only twenty riders and forcibly seized civilian livestock for the march.

sentences.zh: 至咸陽，蕃軍已過渭水。

translations.literal: When he reached Xianyang, the Tibetan army had already crossed the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Xianyang, the Tibetans had crossed the Wei.

sentences.zh: 其日，天子避狄幸陜州。

translations.literal: That day the Son of Heaven fled the barbarians to Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor fled east to Shaanzhou before the invaders.

sentences.zh: 子儀聞上避狄，雪涕還京，至則車駕已發。

translations.literal: Ziyi, hearing the emperor's flight, wept through snow and returned to the capital; when he arrived the imperial carriage had already departed.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the flight, Ziyi wept and raced back to Chang'an, but the imperial train was already gone.

sentences.zh: 射生將王獻忠從駕，沿路遂以四百騎叛，仍逼豐王已下十王欲投於賊。

translations.literal: The archer-captain Wang Xianzhong, accompanying the carriage, rebelled along the route with four hundred horsemen and even forced the Prince of Feng and nine other princes toward the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Archer-captain Wang Xianzhong, escorting the court, mutinied with four hundred riders and tried to deliver the Prince of Feng and nine other princes to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 子儀入開遠門，遇之，詰豐王等所向，遂護送行在。

translations.literal: Ziyi entered the Kaiyuan Gate, met them, questioned where the Prince of Feng and the others were headed, and escorted them to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi entered Kaiyuan Gate, intercepted them, demanded their destination, and escorted the princes to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 子儀以三千騎傍南山，至商州，得武關防兵及六軍散卒四千人，招輯亡逸，其軍漸振。

translations.literal: Ziyi with three thousand horsemen followed the southern hills to Shangzhou, gathered Wuguan garrison troops and four thousand scattered men of the Six Armies, rallied the fugitives, and his force gradually revived.
translations.idiomatic: With three thousand riders he traced the southern hills to Shangzhou, collected Wuguan guards and four thousand stragglers, and slowly rebuilt his army.

sentences.zh: 蕃犯京城，得故邠王守禮子廣武王承宏，立帝號，假署百官。

translations.literal: When Tibet invaded the capital, they obtained the former Prince of Bin Wang Shouli's son the Prince of Guangwu Cheng Hong, set up an imperial title, and falsely appointed the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans found Cheng Hong, son of the former Prince of Bin, proclaimed him emperor, and installed a puppet bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 子儀遣六軍兵馬使張知節、烏崇福、羽林軍使長孫全緒等將兵萬人為前鋒，營於韓公堆，盛張旗幟，鼓鞞震山谷。

translations.literal: Ziyi sent the Six Armies commissioners Zhang Zhijie, Wu Chongfu, and Imperial Guard commissioner Changsun Quanxu and others to lead ten thousand men as vanguard, encamping at Han Gongdui, displaying banners until drums shook the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Zhijie, Wu Chongfu, and Changsun Quanxu with ten thousand vanguard troops to Han Gongdui, where banners and drums filled the valleys.

sentences.zh: 全緒遣禁軍舊將王甫入長安，陰結少年豪俠以為內應，一日，齊擊鼓於硃雀街，蕃軍惶駭而去。

translations.literal: Quanxu sent the former palace guard officer Wang Fu into Chang'an to secretly rally young bravos as inside allies; one day they beat drums together on Zhuque Street and the Tibetan army fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Changsun Quanxu sent Wang Fu into the city to organize young allies; one day drums rolled on Zhuque Street and the Tibetans fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 大將李忠義先屯兵苑中，渭北節度使王仲升守朝堂。

translations.literal: Great general Li Zhongyi first garrisoned the park; Weibei military commissioner Wang Zhongsheng held the audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongyi held the imperial park; Weibei commissioner Wang Zhongsheng guarded the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 子儀以大軍續進，至浐西。

translations.literal: Ziyi followed with the main army to the west of Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi advanced the main body to west of Chan.

sentences.zh: 射生將王撫自署為京兆尹，聚兵二千人，擾亂京城，子儀召撫殺之。

translations.literal: The archer-captain Wang Fu styled himself metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, gathered two thousand men, and disturbed the capital; Ziyi summoned and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu declared himself Jingzhao governor, raised two thousand men, and terrorized the city until Ziyi had him killed.

sentences.zh: 詔子儀權京城留守。

translations.literal: An edict made Ziyi acting capital intendant.
translations.idiomatic: The throne named Ziyi acting defender of the capital.

sentences.zh: 自西蕃入寇，車駕東幸，天下皆咎程元振，諫官屢論之。

translations.literal: Since the western barbarians invaded, the imperial carriage had gone east and all under heaven blamed Cheng Yuanzhen; remonstrating officials repeatedly indicted him.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tibetan invasion and the emperor's flight east, the empire blamed Cheng Yuanzhen; censors repeatedly attacked him.

sentences.zh: 元振懼，又以子儀復立功，不欲天子還京，勸帝且都洛陽以避蕃冠，代宗然之，下詔有日。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen feared this, and because Ziyi might win merit again, did not want the Son of Heaven to return to the capital; he urged the emperor to establish the court at Luoyang to avoid the Tibetan threat, and Daizong agreed; an edict was imminent.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing indictment and fearing Ziyi's renewed glory, Yuanzhen urged moving the court to Luoyang to escape Tibet; Daizong agreed and an edict was drafted.

sentences.zh: 子儀聞之，因兵部侍郎張重光宣慰回，附章論奏曰：

translations.literal: Ziyi heard of this and, as Vice Minister of War Zhang Chongguang returned from a consolation mission, attached a memorial arguing:
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi learned of the plan and, when Vice Minister Zhang Chongguang returned from a mission, appended a memorial arguing:

sentences.zh: 臣聞雍州之地，古稱天府，右探隴、蜀，左扼崤、函，前有終南、太華之險，後有清渭、濁河之固，神明之奧，王者所都。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the land of Yongzhou was anciently called the Heavenly Storehouse—on the right reaching Long and Shu, on the left gripping Xiao and Han, with the peril of Zhongnan and Taihua before and the solidity of the clear Wei and muddy Yellow River behind—the abode of the spirits where kings reside.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou, the ancient 'Heavenly Storehouse,' reaches Long and Shu on the right and Xiao and Han on the left, with Zhongnan and Taihua before it and the Wei and Yellow rivers behind—the seat of kings blessed by the spirits.

sentences.zh: 地方數千里，帶甲十余萬，兵強士勇，雄視八方，有利則出攻，無利則入守。

translations.literal: Its territory spans several thousand li, with more than one hundred thousand armored men, strong soldiers and brave officers, dominating eight directions—when there is advantage they strike out, when not they withdraw and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of li wide, with over one hundred thousand armored men—it dominates the realm, attacking when strong and retreating when not.

sentences.zh: 此用武之國，非諸夏所同，秦、漢因之，卒成帝業。

translations.literal: This is a land for wielding arms, not the same as the other Chinese regions; Qin and Han relied on it and finally achieved imperial enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: It is a land made for war unlike the eastern heartland; Qin and Han built empires from it.

sentences.zh: 其後或處之而泰，去之而亡，前史所書，不唯一姓。

translations.literal: Afterward, sometimes holding it brought peace, leaving it brought ruin—the former histories record this for more than one house.
translations.idiomatic: History shows that holding it brought peace and abandoning it brought ruin—not once alone.

sentences.zh: 及隋氏季末，煬帝南遷，河、洛丘墟，兵戈亂起。

translations.literal: When the Sui dynasty neared its end, Emperor Yang moved south; the Yellow River and Luoyang became wasteland and weapons of war rose everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: At the Sui's fall Emperor Yang fled south; Luoyang lay in ruins and war spread.

sentences.zh: 高祖唱義，亦先入關，惟能翦滅奸雄，底定區宇。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu raised righteousness and likewise entered the Pass first, for he alone could cut down traitors and settle the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu too entered the Pass first and cut down traitors to settle the realm.

sentences.zh: 以至於太宗、高宗之盛，中宗、玄宗之明，多在秦川，鮮居東洛。

translations.literal: Down to the splendor of Taizong and Gaozong and the clarity of Zhongzong and Xuanzong, most dwelt in Qinchuan and rarely lived in eastern Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: From Taizong and Gaozong through Zhongzong and Xuanzong, emperors mostly ruled from Qinchuan, not Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 間者羯胡構亂，九服分崩，河北、河南，盡從逆命。

translations.literal: Recently the Jie barbarians stirred rebellion and the nine domains split; Hebei and Henan all followed the rebels' orders.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jie rebels rose, the nine domains shattered and Hebei and Henan obeyed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 然而先帝仗朔方之眾，慶緒奔亡；

translations.literal: Yet the late emperor relied on Shuofang's forces and Qingxu fled;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the late emperor's Shuofang armies drove Qingxu to flight;

sentences.zh: 陛下藉西土之師，朝義就戮。

translations.literal: Your Majesty borrowed western armies and Chaoyi was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's western troops brought Chaoyi to execution.

sentences.zh: 豈唯天道助順，抑亦地形使然，此陛下所知，非臣飾說。

translations.literal: Was it only heaven aiding the righteous? It was also terrain—this Your Majesty knows; it is not my embellishment.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven helped the righteous, but terrain mattered too—you know this; I do not flatter.

sentences.zh: 近因吐蕃淩逼，鑾駕東巡。

translations.literal: Recently, because Tibet pressed hard, the imperial carriage toured east.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Tibet pressed the capital and the court fled east.

sentences.zh: 蓋以六軍之兵，素非精練，皆市肆屠沽之人，務掛虛名，茍避征賦，及驅以就戰，百無一堪。

translations.literal: It is because the Six Armies were never well trained—mostly market butchers and peddlers seeking empty titles to dodge taxes; when driven to battle, not one in a hundred was usable.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Armies were never trained—mostly peddlers dodging taxes; in battle scarcely one in a hundred could fight.

sentences.zh: 亦有潛輸貨財，因以求免。

translations.literal: Some secretly paid bribes to buy exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Some bought their way out with bribes.

sentences.zh: 又中官掩蔽，庶政多荒。

translations.literal: Eunuchs concealed wrongdoing and many policies lay waste.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs hid abuses and government rotted.

sentences.zh: 遂令陛下振蕩不安，退居陜服。

translations.literal: Thus Your Majesty was shaken and unsettled, withdrawing to Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Your Majesty was driven out to Shaan.

sentences.zh: 斯蓋關於委任失所，豈可謂秦地非良者哉！

translations.literal: This concerns mistaken appointments—how can one say the Qin land is not good!
translations.idiomatic: That was bad appointments—not proof that Chang'an is unsound!

sentences.zh: 今道路云云，不知信否，咸謂陛下已有成命，將幸洛都。

translations.literal: Now the roads buzz with rumor, unsure whether true, all saying Your Majesty has already decided and will go to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors say Your Majesty has decided on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 臣熟思其端，未見其利。

translations.literal: Your subject has thought hard at the root and sees no profit.
translations.idiomatic: I have weighed the move and see no gain.

sentences.zh: 夫以東周之地，久陷賊中，宮室焚燒，十不存一。

translations.literal: As for the land of eastern Zhou, long fallen to rebels, palaces burned—not one in ten remains.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Zhou lands, long in rebel hands, are burned—nine palaces in ten gone.

sentences.zh: 百曹荒廢，曾無尺椽，中間畿內，不滿千戶。

translations.literal: The hundred offices lie waste without a single beam; within the capital district barely a thousand households remain.
translations.idiomatic: Offices are empty without a beam; inside the walls barely a thousand households survive.

sentences.zh: 井邑榛荊，豺狼站嗥，既乏軍儲，又鮮人力，東至鄭、汴，達於徐方，北自覃懷，經於相土，人煙斷絕，千里蕭條。

translations.literal: Hamlets are choked with thorns, wolves howl; military stores are lacking and manpower scarce; from Zheng and Bian east to Xufang, north from Tanhuai through Xiangtu, human smoke is cut off and a thousand li are desolate.
translations.idiomatic: Thorns choke the towns, wolves howl, stores are gone and hands are few—from Zheng and Bian to Xuzhou, from Tanhuai to Xiangtu, the land is empty for a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 將何以奉萬乘之牲餼，供百官之次舍？

translations.literal: How then will you supply the myriad chariots' sacrificial beasts and lodge the hundred officials?
translations.idiomatic: How will you feed imperial sacrifices or house the bureaucracy?

sentences.zh: 矧其土地狹厄，才數百里間，東有成臯，南有二室，險不足恃，適為戰場。

translations.literal: Moreover the land is narrow and cramped, only several hundred li across; east lies Chenggao, south the Two Rooms—the passes are not enough to rely on and only suit a battlefield.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's ground is narrow—Chenggao east, Song peaks south—defenses weak, fit only for battle.

sentences.zh: 陛下奈何棄久安之勢，從至危之策，忽社稷之計，生天下之心。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, why abandon long security for the utmost peril, neglect the altars' plan, and stir the hearts of all under heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Why abandon long security for peril, neglect the dynasty, and unsettle the empire?

sentences.zh: 臣雖至愚，竊為陛下不取。

translations.literal: Though your subject is extremely foolish, I privately deem this unwise for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Forgive my bluntness—I beg you not to take this course.

sentences.zh: 代宗省表，垂泣謂左右曰：「子儀用心，真社稷臣也。

translations.literal: Daizong read the memorial, wept, and told those beside him, "Ziyi's intent—truly he is a minister of the altars."
translations.idiomatic: Reading it, Daizong wept and said, "Ziyi's heart is truly that of a pillar of state."

sentences.zh: 可亟還京師。

translations.literal: Return quickly to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Return to Chang'an at once."

sentences.zh: 」十一月，車駕自陜還宮，子儀伏地請罪，帝駐車勞之曰：「朕用卿不早，故及於此。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the imperial carriage returned from Shaan to the palace; Ziyi prostrated himself to beg forgiveness; the emperor halted the carriage to comfort him, saying, "I did not employ you early enough, and so came to this."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the court returned; Ziyi kowtowed for blame; the emperor stopped to say, "I used you too late, and this befell us."

sentences.zh: 」乃賜鐵券，圖形淩煙閣。

translations.literal: He then granted an iron certificate and had his image placed in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He granted an iron certificate and ordered Ziyi's portrait in the Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 是時，河北副元帥仆固懷恩方頓軍汾州，掠並、汾諸縣以為己邑。

translations.literal: At that time the Hebei deputy commander-in-chief Pugu Huai'en was encamped at Fenzhou, plundering Bing and Fen counties as his own domains.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Pugu Huai'en camped at Fenzhou, looting Bing and Fen as private fief.

sentences.zh: 乃以子儀兼關內河東副元帥、河中節度觀察使，出鎮河中。

translations.literal: Ziyi was then made concurrent deputy commander-in-chief of Guannei and Hedong and Hezhong observation commissioner, and sent to garrison Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi was named deputy commander of Guannei and Hedong and commissioner of Hezhong, and sent to garrison there.

sentences.zh: 蕃戎既退，仆固懷恩部下離散。

translations.literal: After the barbarian armies withdrew, Pugu Huai'en's followers scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When the invaders withdrew, Huai'en's men scattered.

sentences.zh: 是月，懷恩子瑒主兵榆次，為帳下將張惟嶽所殺，傳首京師。

translations.literal: That month Huai'en's son Chang commanded troops at Yuci and was killed by his officer Zhang Weiyue; the head was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That month Huai'en's son Chang held Yuci until officer Zhang Weiyue killed him and sent his head to court.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽以瑒之眾歸於子儀，懷恩懼，棄其母而走靈州。

translations.literal: Weiyue brought Chang's force to Ziyi; Huai'en feared, abandoned his mother, and fled to Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue surrendered Chang's troops to Ziyi; Huai'en fled to Lingzhou, abandoning even his mother.

sentences.zh: 明年九月，以子儀守太尉，充北道邠寧、涇原、河西已東通和蕃及朔方招撫觀察使，其關內河東副元帥、中書令如故。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the following year, Ziyi was made Defender-in-Chief and commissioner to pacify and observe Binning, Jingyuan, Hexi east of the line, allied Tibetan areas, and Shuofang on the northern route, retaining his posts as deputy commander-in-chief of Guannei and Hedong and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Next ninth month he became Defender-in-Chief and pacification commissioner for Binning, Jingyuan, Hexi, allied Tibetans, and Shuofang, keeping his deputy commander and grand councilor titles.

sentences.zh: 子儀以懷恩未誅，不宜讓使，堅辭太尉，曰：「太尉職雄任重，竊憂非據，輒敢上聞。

translations.literal: Ziyi, because Huai'en was not yet executed, deemed it improper to accept the envoy post and firmly declined the Defender-in-Chief, saying, "The Defender-in-Chief's office is mighty and its burden heavy; I privately fear I am unfit and dare report upward."
translations.idiomatic: With Huai'en still at large, Ziyi refused the Defender-in-Chief post, writing, "The office is too weighty for me—I dare report my unfitness."

sentences.zh: 伏奉詔書，未允誠懇。

translations.literal: I received the edict, yet my sincere plea was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Your edict came, yet my plea was denied.

sentences.zh: 臣疇昔之分，早知止足，今茲累請，竊懼滿盈。

translations.literal: Your subject long knew my proper limit; now these repeated requests—I privately fear overflowing.
translations.idiomatic: I have long known my limits; repeated refusal fears hubris.

sentences.zh: 義實由衷，事非矯飾，誌之所至，敢不盡言。

translations.literal: The righteousness is truly from the heart; the matter is not pretense; where my will reaches, I dare not speak less than fully.
translations.idiomatic: This is sincere, not show; I must speak fully.

sentences.zh: 自兵亂已來，紀綱浸壞，時多躁競，俗少廉隅。

translations.literal: Since the military chaos began, discipline has gradually decayed; the age is full of rash rivalry and short on integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Since rebellion, discipline has rotted; men scramble for rank and lack integrity.

sentences.zh: 德薄而位尊，功微而賞厚，實繁有眾，不可殫論。

translations.literal: Thin virtue yet high rank, slight merit yet rich reward—truly many are the cases, not all can be told.
translations.idiomatic: Many hold high rank with thin virtue and rich reward for slight merit—too many to list.

sentences.zh: 臣每見之，深以為念。

translations.literal: Each time I see this, I deeply reflect on it.
translations.idiomatic: Each time I see it, I shudder.

sentences.zh: 昔范宣子讓，其下皆讓，欒騕為汰，不敢違也。

translations.literal: Formerly when Fan Xuanzi yielded, those below all yielded; Luan Yao was dissolute and dared not disobey.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Xuanzi yielded, others yielded; even the dissolute Luan Yao dared not refuse.

sentences.zh: 臣誠薄劣，竊慕古人，務欲以身率先，大變浮俗，是用勤勤懇懇，願罷此官，庶禮讓興行，由臣而致也。

translations.literal: Your subject is truly thin and inferior, yet I privately admire the ancients and wish to take the lead myself in greatly changing floating custom; therefore I am earnest and sincere in begging to resign this office, that courtesy and yielding may rise through me.
translations.idiomatic: I am unworthy yet imitate the ancients, hoping my example might restore modesty—thus I beg to resign.

sentences.zh: 臣位為上相，爵為真王，參啟沃之謀，受腹心之寄，恩榮已極，功業已成，尋合乞骸，保全余齒。

translations.literal: Your subject's rank is chief minister, his title a true prince; I share in nurturing counsel and bear the trust of the heart; grace and glory have reached their peak and achievement is complete—I ought soon to beg to retire and preserve my remaining years.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister and true prince I share the dynasty's secrets; honors are complete—I should retire in peace.

sentences.zh: 但以冠仇在近，家國未安，臣子之心，不敢寧處。

translations.literal: But because the barbarian foe is near and house and state are not yet secure, the heart of a subject dare not rest at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet with barbarians near and the realm unsettled, a loyal subject cannot rest.

sentences.zh: 茍西戎即敘，懷恩就擒，疇昔官爵，誓無所受，必當追蹤范蠡，繼跡留侯。

translations.literal: If the western barbarians soon submit and Huai'en is captured, for my former ranks and titles I swear to accept none; I shall surely follow Fan Li and tread in Zhang Liang's footsteps.
translations.idiomatic: If Tibet submits and Huai'en is taken, I will accept no former rank and follow Fan Li and Zhang Liang into retirement.

sentences.zh: 臣之鄙懷，切在於此。

translations.literal: Your subject's humble intent lies urgently in this.
translations.idiomatic: That is my earnest wish.

sentences.zh: 」優詔不許。

translations.literal: A gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: A gentle edict refused.

sentences.zh: 子儀見上，感泣懇讓，乃止。

translations.literal: When Ziyi saw the emperor, moved to tears he earnestly declined and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor, Ziyi wept and pleaded until he desisted.

sentences.zh: 十月，仆固懷恩引吐蕃、回紇、党項數十萬南下，京師大恐，子儀出鎮奉天。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Pugu Huai'en led several hundred thousand Tibetans, Uyghurs, and Tangut tribes south; the capital was greatly alarmed, and Ziyi went out to garrison Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Huai'en led hundreds of thousands of Tibetans, Uyghurs, and Tanguts south; the capital panicked and Ziyi marched to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 帝召子儀問禦戎之計，子儀曰：「以臣所見，懷恩無能為也。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Ziyi to ask his plan for repelling the barbarians; Ziyi said, "In your subject's view, Huai'en can do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Daizong asked his plan; Ziyi said, "Huai'en cannot succeed."

sentences.zh: 」帝問其故，對曰：「懷恩雖稱驍勇，素失士心，今所以能為亂者，引思歸之人耳。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the reason; he replied, "Though Huai'en is called fierce and brave, he has long lost the soldiers' hearts; what enables him to make trouble now is that he leads men who long to return home."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said, "Huai'en is fierce but has lost his army; he only leads homesick men."

sentences.zh: 懷恩本臣偏將，其下皆臣之部曲，臣恩信嘗及之，今臣為大將，必不忍以鋒刃相向，以此知其無能為也。

translations.literal: Huai'en was originally my subordinate general; those below were all my troops; my favor and trust once reached them; now as great general I surely cannot bear to turn blades against them—by this I know he can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was my subordinate; his men are still my old troops, and I cannot bear to cut them down—that is why he will fail.

sentences.zh: 」虜寇邠州，子儀在涇陽，子儀令長男朔方兵馬使曜率師援之，與邠寧節度使白孝德閉城拒守。

translations.literal: The barbarians raided Binzhou; Ziyi was at Jingyang; he ordered his eldest son, Shuofang army commissioner Yao, to lead troops to aid, and with Binning commissioner Bai Xiaode they closed the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders hit Binzhou, Ziyi at Jingyang sent his son Yao with Shuofang troops to help Bai Xiaode hold the walls.

sentences.zh: 懷恩前鋒至奉天，近城挑戰，諸將請擊之，子儀止之曰：「夫客兵深入，利在速戰，不可爭鋒。

translations.literal: Huai'en's vanguard reached Fengtian and challenged near the walls; the generals asked to strike; Ziyi stopped them, saying, "An invading army deep inside profits from quick battle—we must not contend at the spear point."
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en's vanguard taunted Fengtian; officers wanted to fight, but Ziyi said invaders profit from speed and forbade a clash.

sentences.zh: 彼皆吾之部曲，緩之自當攜貳；

translations.literal: They are all my old troops; if we go slowly they will naturally split in two;
translations.idiomatic: They are my own men; delay will turn them against Huai'en;

sentences.zh: 若迫之，是速其戰，戰則勝負未可知。

translations.literal: if we press them, we hasten battle, and victory or defeat cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: pressure forces battle, and the outcome is uncertain.

sentences.zh: 敢言戰者斬！

translations.literal: Whoever dares speak of battle—behead him!
translations.idiomatic: Whoever speaks of fighting—behead him!

sentences.zh: 」堅壁待之，果不戰而退。

translations.literal: He held the walls and waited; as expected they did not fight and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He held fast; they never fought and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 子儀自涇陽入朝，帝御安福門待之，命子儀樓上行朝見之禮，宴賜隆厚。

translations.literal: Ziyi came to court from Jingyang; the emperor waited at the Anfu Gate; he ordered Ziyi to perform court ceremony on the tower, with a lavish feast and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: From Jingyang he was received at Anfu Gate with ceremony on the tower and a lavish feast.

sentences.zh: 十一月，以子儀為尚書令，上表懇辭曰：「臣以薄劣，素乏行能，逢時擾攘，猥蒙驅策，內參朝政，外總兵權。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Ziyi was made Director of the Imperial Secretariat; he memorialized earnestly declining, saying, "Your subject is thin and inferior, by nature lacking conduct and ability; meeting a time of turmoil, I unworthily received driving and deployment, within sharing court governance, without commanding military power overall."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was named Director of the Imperial Secretariat and declined, citing unworthiness in an age of turmoil where he had shared civil and military power.

sentences.zh: 上不能翼戴三光，下不能糾逖群慝，功微賞厚，任重恩深，覆餗之憂，實盈寤寐。

translations.literal: Above I could not wing and bear the three luminaries; below I could not correct distant wickedness; merit slight yet reward thick, burden heavy yet grace deep—the worry of overturning the pot truly fills waking and sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: I neither upheld heaven's light nor checked evil; reward outran merit and grace outweighed service—I live in fear of failure.

sentences.zh: 臣昨所以固辭太尉，乞保余年，殊私曲臨，遂見矜許。

translations.literal: Your subject yesterday therefore firmly declined the Defender-in-Chief and begged to preserve my remaining years; special favor bent close and thus saw me commended.
translations.idiomatic: I refused the Defender-in-Chief to preserve my old age, and Your Majesty kindly agreed.

sentences.zh: 竊謂陛下已知其願，深察其心，豈意未歷旬時，復延寵命。

translations.literal: I privately thought Your Majesty already knew my wish and deeply discerned my heart—who would have thought that before ten days had passed you would again extend a favored appointment.
translations.idiomatic: I thought you understood my wish—yet within ten days came another honor.

sentences.zh: 以臣褊淺，又寡智謀，安可謬職南宮，當茲大任？

translations.literal: With your subject narrow and shallow, again lacking wisdom and plan, how can I wrongly hold office in the Southern Palace at such a great charge?
translations.idiomatic: I am narrow and unwise—how can I hold the Southern Palace at such a charge?

sentences.zh: 況太宗昔居籓邸，嘗踐此官，累聖相承，曠而不置。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Taizong formerly dwelt in the princely residence he once held this office; successive sacred emperors inherited it and left it vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once held this office as prince; later emperors left it empty by tradition.

sentences.zh: 皇太子為雍王之日，陛下以其總兵薄伐，平定關東，飲至策勛，再有斯授。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was Prince of Yong, Your Majesty because he commanded troops in the thin campaign and pacified Guandong, at the drinking ceremony recording merit, again made this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was Prince of Yong, you gave him this office after he pacified Guandong.

sentences.zh: 豈臣末職，敢亂大倫？

translations.literal: How could your subject, in a low post, dare disorder the great relations?
translations.idiomatic: How can a lesser man like me disturb that precedent?

sentences.zh: 德薄位尊，難逃天子之責；

translations.literal: Thin virtue yet high rank—hard to escape the Son of Heaven's blame;
translations.idiomatic: Thin virtue and high rank invite the emperor's rebuke;

sentences.zh: 負乘致冠，復速神明之誅。

translations.literal: bearing unfit load and inviting the crown—again hastening the spirits' punishment.
translations.idiomatic: unfit office invites heaven's punishment.

sentences.zh: 伏乞天慈，俯停新命。

translations.literal: I beg heaven's kindness to bend and halt the new appointment.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to withdraw this appointment.

sentences.zh: 」答詔不允。

translations.literal: The reply edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict refused.

sentences.zh: 翌日，敕所司令子儀於尚書省視事。

translations.literal: The next day, an edict ordered the relevant offices to have Ziyi attend to business at the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he was ordered to take up duty at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 詔宰相百僚送上，遣射生五百騎執戟翼從，自朝堂至省，賜教坊樂。

translations.literal: An edict had the chief councilors and hundred officials escort him up; five hundred archer-captain horsemen with halberds flanked him from the court hall to the ministry, granting Music Bureau performers.
translations.idiomatic: Councilors escorted him with five hundred halberd-bearing guards and Music Bureau performers from court to ministry.

sentences.zh: 子儀不受，復上表曰：

translations.literal: Ziyi did not accept and again memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He refused again and memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣伏以尚書令，武德之際，太宗為之，昨瀝懇上陳，請罷斯職；

translations.literal: Your subject reflects that the Director of the Imperial Secretariat—in the Wude era Taizong held it; yesterday I poured out earnest words above and asked to abolish this office;
translations.idiomatic: The Director's post—Taizong held it in Wude; yesterday I asked to abolish it;

sentences.zh: 而陛下未垂亮察，務欲褒崇，區區微誠，益用惶懼。

translations.literal: yet Your Majesty did not bend clear sight, insisting on praise and elevation; my tiny sincerity grows ever more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: yet you insist on honoring me, and my fear grows.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 太宗立極之主，聖德在人，自後因廢此官，永代作則。

translations.literal: Taizong was an enthroned ruler, sage virtue in men; afterward this office was abolished as an eternal model for generations.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong abolished this office as a model for all time.

sentences.zh: 陛下守文繼體，固當奉而行之，豈可猥私老臣，隳厥成式，上掩陛下之德，下貽萬方之非。

translations.literal: Your Majesty guards the text and inherits the body—you should surely follow and execute it; how can you unworthily favor an old subject, destroy that established form, cover Your Majesty's virtue above, and leave wrong for ten thousand directions below?
translations.idiomatic: You should follow that precedent, not favor me and stain your virtue and the empire's norms.

sentences.zh: 臣雖至愚，安敢輕受？

translations.literal: Though your subject is extremely foolish, how dare I lightly accept?
translations.idiomatic: How dare I accept lightly?

sentences.zh: 況久經兵亂，僭賞者多，一人之身，兼官數四，硃紫同色，清濁不分，「爛羊」之謠，復聞聖代。

translations.literal: Moreover, after long military chaos, many received excessive rewards; one man's body holds several concurrent offices at once, vermilion and purple the same color, clear and turbid undivided—the 'rotten sheep' ballad is heard again in a sacred age.
translations.idiomatic: After long war, offices pile on one man, ranks blur, and the 'rotten sheep' satire returns even in a sage reign.

sentences.zh: 臣頃觀其弊，思革其源，以逆寇猶存，未敢輕議。
