translations.literal: Your subject recently observed these ills and thought to reform their source; because the rebel bandits still existed, I did not dare lightly discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: I saw these abuses but stayed silent while rebels remained.

sentences.zh: 今元兇沮敗，計日成擒，中外無虞，妖氛漸息。

translations.literal: Now the arch-criminal is thwarted and defeated, capture counted by days; within and without there is no worry, and the evil miasma gradually subsides.
translations.idiomatic: Now the chief rebel nears capture and the realm calms.

sentences.zh: 此陛下作法之際，審官之時，固合始於老臣，化及班列。

translations.literal: This is the time when Your Majesty makes law and examines officials—you should surely begin with this old subject and extend the change to the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: This is the moment to reform ranks—begin with me.

sentences.zh: 豈可輕為此舉，以亂國章？

translations.literal: How can you lightly make this act and disorder the state's statutes?
translations.idiomatic: Do not disorder the state's statutes for my sake.

sentences.zh: 國章亂於上，則庶政隳於下，海內之政皆亂，則國家又安得永代而無患哉！

translations.literal: When state statutes are disordered above, then the hundred policies are ruined below; when policies throughout the seas are disordered, how can the state forever be without calamity!
translations.idiomatic: If statutes break at the top, government collapses below and the dynasty cannot endure.

sentences.zh: 陛下茍能從臣之言，俯察誠請，彼貪榮冒進者，亦將各讓其所兼之官，自然天下文明，百工式敘，太平之業，可得而復也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty can follow your subject's words, bend to examine my sincere plea, those who greedily honor and rashly advance will also yield their concurrent offices; naturally all under heaven will be civilized, the hundred crafts ordered, and the enterprise of great peace can be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: If you heed me, the greedy will yield extra offices and good order may return.

sentences.zh: 臣誠蒙鄙，識昧古今，誌之所切，實在於此。

translations.literal: Your subject is truly crude and low, knowledge dim on past and present; where my will cuts, it urgently lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: My earnest wish lies here alone.

sentences.zh: 手詔答曰：「優崇之命，所以報功；

translations.literal: The hand-edict replied: "The favor of elevation is to repay merit;
translations.idiomatic: The reply said: "This honor repays merit;

sentences.zh: 總領之司，期於賦政。

translations.literal: the department of overall charge expects to assign governance.
translations.idiomatic: this office expects governance."

sentences.zh: 卿入居臺鉉，出統戎旃，爰自先朝，累匡多難，靖群氛於海表，凝庶績於天階。

translations.literal: You enter to occupy the platform and axe, go out to command the military banners—from the former court, repeatedly aiding in many hardships, pacifying the evil miasma beyond the seas, consolidating the myriad achievements on heaven's steps.
translations.idiomatic: You have served civil and military roles since the former reign, pacifying the realm.

sentences.zh: 敏事而寡言，居敬而行簡，人難其易，爾易其難。

translations.literal: Quick in affairs yet sparing in words, dwelling in reverence yet acting simply—others find the easy hard; you find the hard easy.
translations.idiomatic: You act swiftly yet speak little—others find easy tasks hard, you the reverse.

sentences.zh: 所以命掌六聯，首茲百辟，顧循時議，僉謂允諧。

translations.literal: Therefore I appoint you to manage the six departments, first among the hundred ministers; looking to current opinion, all say it is fitting and harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Hence you head the six ministries, and opinion calls it fitting.

sentences.zh: 而屢拜封章，懇懷讓揖，守淳素之道，語政理之源，無待禮成，曲從德讓。

translations.literal: Yet you repeatedly bow with sealed memorials, earnest in yielding courtesy, keeping the way of pure simplicity, speaking of the source of governing principle—without waiting for the rites to be complete, I bend to follow virtue's yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Your repeated refusals show virtue; I yield to your modesty.

sentences.zh: 宜宣示於外，編之史冊。

translations.literal: It should be proclaimed abroad and compiled in the historical records.
translations.idiomatic: Let this be proclaimed and recorded.

sentences.zh: 」遣內侍魚朝恩傳詔，賜美人盧氏等六人、從者八人，並車服、帷帳、床蓐、珍玩之具。

translations.literal: He sent the inner attendant Yu Chao'en to transmit the edict, granting the beauties the Lu clan and six others, eight attendants, and equipage, curtains, bedding, and precious playthings.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chao'en delivered the edict with six concubines, eight attendants, and rich furnishings.

sentences.zh: 時蕃虜屢寇京畿，倚蒲、陜為內地，常以重兵鎮之。

translations.literal: At that time the barbarians repeatedly raided the capital region; relying on Pu and Shaan as inner lands, heavy troops were usually garrisoned there.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians repeatedly raided the capital; heavy garrisons held Pu and Shaan.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年五月，以子儀都統河南道節度行營，出鎮河中。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yongtai, Ziyi was made overall commander of the Henan circuit field army and went out to garrison Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 1, fifth month, he took command of Henan field armies at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 八月，仆固懷恩誘吐蕃、回紇、党項、羌、渾、奴剌，山賊任敷、鄭庭、郝德、劉開元等三十余萬南下，先發數萬人掠同州，期自華陰趨藍田，以扼南路，懷恩率重兵繼其後。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Pugu Huai'en incited Tibet, Uyghurs, Tanguts, Qiang, Hun, and Nula tribes, mountain bandits Ren Fu, Zheng Ting, Hao De, Liu Kaiyuan, and others—more than three hundred thousand southward; he first sent tens of thousands to plunder Tongzhou, planning from Huayin toward Lantian to choke the southern road, with Huai'en leading heavy troops following after.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Huai'en stirred Tibet, Uyghurs, Tanguts, and over three hundred thousand allies south—first looting Tongzhou toward Lantian while he followed with the main host.

sentences.zh: 回紇、吐蕃自涇、邠、鳳翔數道寇京畿，掠奉天、醴泉。

translations.literal: Uyghurs and Tibet from Jing, Bin, and Fengxiang on several routes raided the capital region, plundering Fengtian and Liquan.
translations.idiomatic: Uyghurs and Tibet raided from several routes, looting Fengtian and Liquan.

sentences.zh: 京師震恐，天子下詔親征，命李忠臣屯東渭橋，李光進屯雲陽，馬璘、郝廷玉屯便橋，駱奉先、李日越屯盩啡，李抱玉屯鳳翔。

translations.literal: The capital shook with fear; the Son of Heaven issued an edict for personal campaign; Li Zhongchen was ordered to garrison East Wei Bridge, Li Guangjin at Yunyang, Ma Lin and Hao Tingyu at Bian Bridge, Luo Fengxian and Li Yueyue at Zhouzhi, Li Baoyu at Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered personal campaign; Li Zhongchen, Li Guangjin, Ma Lin, and others took assigned posts around the capital.

sentences.zh: 周智光屯同州，杜冕屯坊州，天子以禁軍屯苑內。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhiguang garrisoned Tongzhou, Du Mian garrisoned Fangzhou; the Son of Heaven stationed palace guards within the park.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhiguang held Tongzhou, Du Mian Fangzhou, palace guards the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 京城壯丁，並令團結。

translations.literal: Able-bodied men of the capital were all ordered to form militia.
translations.idiomatic: Capital militia were mobilized.

sentences.zh: 城二門塞其一。

translations.literal: One of the city's two gates was blocked shut.
translations.idiomatic: One city gate was sealed.

sentences.zh: 魚朝恩括士庶私馬，重兵捉城門，市民由竇穴而遁去，人情危迫。

translations.literal: Yu Chao'en requisitioned private horses from gentry and commoners; heavy troops guarded the gates; citizens escaped through holes; human sentiment was urgent and pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chao'en seized private horses and locked the gates until people fled through holes in panic.

sentences.zh: 是時，急召子儀自河中至，屯於涇陽，而虜騎已合。

translations.literal: At that time Ziyi was urgently summoned from Hezhong, encamped at Jingyang, and the barbarian horsemen had already joined.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi was rushed from Hezhong to Jingyang as enemy cavalry converged.

sentences.zh: 子儀一軍萬余人，而雜虜圍之數重。

translations.literal: Ziyi's one army was a bit more than ten thousand men, while mixed barbarians surrounded them in several rings.
translations.idiomatic: His ten thousand men were ringed by barbarian hosts.

sentences.zh: 子儀使李國臣、高升拒其東，魏楚玉當其南，陳回光當其西，硃元琮當其北。

translations.literal: Ziyi sent Li Guochen and Gao Sheng to block the east, Wei Chuyu the south, Chen Huiguang the west, and Zhu Yuancong the north.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Li Guochen, Gao Sheng, Wei Chuyu, Chen Huiguang, and Zhu Yuancong on four sides.

sentences.zh: 子儀率甲騎二千出沒於左右前後，虜見而問：「此誰也？

translations.literal: Ziyi led two thousand armored horsemen appearing and vanishing left, right, front, and rear; the barbarians saw and asked, "Who is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi rode two thousand armored horsemen back and forth; the enemy asked who he was.

sentences.zh: 」報曰：「郭令公也。

translations.literal: They reported, "It is Duke Guo."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Duke Guo."

sentences.zh: 」回紇曰：「令公存乎？

translations.literal: The Uyghurs said, "Does the Duke still live?"
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs said, "Is the Duke alive?"

sentences.zh: 仆固懷恩言天可汗已棄四海，令公亦謝世，中國無主，故從其來。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en said the Heavenly Khagan had abandoned all under heaven and the Duke had also left the world; China had no lord, therefore we came with him.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en told them the emperor and Duke Guo were dead and China had no ruler.

sentences.zh: 今令公存，天可汗存乎？

translations.literal: Now the Duke lives—does the Heavenly Khagan live?
translations.idiomatic: Now you say the Duke lives—does the emperor live?

sentences.zh: 」報之曰：「皇帝萬歲無疆。

translations.literal: They reported, "The emperor is ten thousand years without bound."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "The emperor lives ten thousand years."

sentences.zh: 」回紇皆曰：「懷恩欺我。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs all said, "Huai'en deceived us."
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs cried, "Huai'en lied!"

sentences.zh: 」子儀又使諭之曰：「公等頃年遠涉萬里，翦除兇逆，恢復二京。

translations.literal: Ziyi again sent to instruct them, saying, "You gentlemen in former years crossed ten thousand li, cut down the fierce and rebellious, and recovered the two capitals."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi sent word: "Years ago you crossed ten thousand li to restore the two capitals with us."

sentences.zh: 是時子儀與公等周旋艱難，何日忘之。

translations.literal: At that time Ziyi with you gentlemen went round in hardship—what day is forgotten?
translations.idiomatic: We shared that hardship—have you forgotten?

sentences.zh: 今忽棄舊好，助一叛臣，何其愚也！

translations.literal: Now you suddenly abandon the old friendship and aid one rebel subject—how extremely foolish!
translations.idiomatic: Why abandon old friendship to aid a rebel?

sentences.zh: 且懷恩背主棄親，於公等何有？

translations.literal: Moreover Huai'en betrayed his lord and abandoned kin—what do you gentlemen have from him?
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en betrayed lord and kin—what do you owe him?

sentences.zh: 」回紇曰：「謂令公亡矣，不然，何以至此。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs said, "We thought the Duke was dead; otherwise, how could we have come to this."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "We thought you dead—else why are we here?"

sentences.zh: 令公誠存，安得而見之？

translations.literal: If the Duke truly lives, how could we see him?
translations.idiomatic: If you live, let us see you."

sentences.zh: 」子儀將出，諸將諫曰：「戎狄之心，不可信也，請無往。

translations.literal: Ziyi was about to go out; the generals remonstrated, saying, "The hearts of the Rong and Di cannot be trusted; please do not go."
translations.idiomatic: Generals warned that barbarians could not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 」子儀曰：「虜有數十倍之眾，今力固不敵，且至誠感神，況虜輩乎！

translations.literal: Ziyi said, "The barbarians have several tens of times our numbers; now our strength truly cannot match; yet utmost sincerity moves the spirits—how much more these barbarian fellows!"
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi said they outnumbered him but sincerity might move them.

sentences.zh: 」諸將曰：「請選鐵騎五百衛從。

translations.literal: The generals said, "Please select five hundred iron horsemen as guard and escort."
translations.idiomatic: They offered five hundred guards.

sentences.zh: 」子儀曰：「適足以為害也。

translations.literal: Ziyi said, "That would just become harm."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi said guards would only provoke harm.

sentences.zh: 」乃傳呼曰：「令公來！

translations.literal: He then called out, "The Duke is coming!"
translations.idiomatic: He called, "The Duke comes!"

sentences.zh: 」虜初疑，持滿註矢以待之。

translations.literal: The barbarians at first doubted, nocked arrows full and waited.
translations.idiomatic: They nocked arrows and waited.

sentences.zh: 子儀以數十騎徐出，免胄而勞之曰：「安乎？

translations.literal: Ziyi with several tens of horsemen slowly came out, removed his helmet, and comforted them, saying, "Are you well? Long together in loyalty and righteousness—how reach this?"
translations.idiomatic: He rode out with a few dozen horsemen, bareheaded, and said, "Are you well? After so long as allies—why this?"

sentences.zh: 久同忠義，何至於是？

translations.literal: The Uyghurs all laid down weapons, dismounted, and bowed together, saying, "Truly he is our father."
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs dropped weapons, dismounted, and bowed as one: "It is truly our father."

sentences.zh: 」回紇皆舍兵下馬齊拜曰：「果吾父也。

translations.literal: Ziyi summoned their chieftains, had each drink wine, gave them gauze and brocade, and spoke joyfully as at first.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned their chiefs, shared wine and brocade, and talked as warmly as in old days.

sentences.zh: 」子儀召其首領，各飲之酒，與之羅錦，歡言如初。

translations.literal: Ziyi persuaded the Uyghurs, saying, "Tibet was originally our uncle-nephew country; coming without obligation is being without kin."
translations.idiomatic: He told the Uyghurs: "Tibet is our marriage kin; they came uninvited—that is to be without family."

sentences.zh: 子儀說回紇曰：「吐蕃本吾舅甥之國，無負而至，是無親也。

translations.literal: If you turn your blades and seize them, it is like picking mustard from the ground.
translations.idiomatic: If you turn your blades on them, victory is as easy as picking greens from the ground.

sentences.zh: 若倒戈乘之，如拾地芥耳。

translations.literal: Their sheep and horses cover the fields for several hundred li—this is called heaven's gift; it cannot be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep and horses cover the plain for hundreds of li—heaven's gift, not to be missed.

sentences.zh: 其羊馬滿野，長數百里，是謂天賜，不可失也。

translations.literal: Now if you can drive off the Rong for profit and return in triumph while renewing friendship with me—is it not good!
translations.idiomatic: Drive the barbarians off for gain, go home in triumph, and renew friendship with us—would that not be best?

sentences.zh: 今能逐戎以利舉，與我繼好而凱旋，不亦善乎！

translations.literal: When Huai'en suddenly died at Mingsha, the mass of barbarians had nothing to command them; they then promised; he sent the chieftain Shiye Na and others to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai'en died suddenly at Mingsha, the tribes lost their leader, agreed to terms, and sent chieftain Shiye Na to court.

sentences.zh: 」會懷恩暴死於鳴沙，群虜無所統攝，遂許諾，乃遣首領石野那等入朝。

translations.literal: Ziyi sent Shuofang army commissioner Bai Yuanguang to join armies with the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi sent Shuofang officer Bai Yuanguang to join the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 子儀遣朔方兵馬使白元光與回紇會軍。

translations.literal: Ziyi sent Shuofang army commissioner Bai Yuanguang to join armies with the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi sent Shuofang officer Bai Yuanguang to join the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃知其謀，是夜奔退。

translations.literal: Tibet learned their plan; that night they fled in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet learned of the plot and fled that night.

sentences.zh: 回紇與元光追之，子儀大軍繼其後，大破吐蕃十余萬於靈武臺西原，斬首五萬，生擒萬人，收其所掠士女四千人，獲牛羊駝馬，三百里內不絕。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs with Yuanguang pursued; Ziyi's great army followed after; they greatly defeated more than one hundred thousand Tibetans west of Lingwu Terrace plain, beheading fifty thousand, capturing ten thousand alive, recovering four thousand men and women they had seized, obtaining sheep, cattle, camels, and horses in an unbroken line for three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Uyghurs and Yuanguang pursued; Ziyi's main force followed and crushed over one hundred thousand Tibetans west of Lingwu, taking fifty thousand heads, ten thousand captives, four thousand rescued civilians, and herds stretching three hundred li.

sentences.zh: 子儀自涇陽入朝，加實封二百戶，還鎮河中。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Dali, Huazhou military commissioner Zhou Zhiguang killed army inspector Zhang Zhibin and plotted rebellion; because the Tong-Hua route was blocked, the emperor summoned Ziyi's son-in-law Vice Minister of Works Zhao Zong to receive an oral edict to go to Hezhong and ordered Ziyi to raise troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 1, twelfth month, Zhou Zhiguang of Huazhou killed inspector Zhang Zhibin and rebelled; the emperor sent Ziyi's son-in-law Zhao Zong with oral orders for Ziyi to attack.

sentences.zh: 大歷元年十二月，華州節度使周智光殺監軍張誌斌謀叛，帝以同、華路阻，召子儀女婿工部侍郎趙縱受口詔往河中，令子儀起軍討之。

translations.literal: Zong asked for a wax-sealed letter and had a household servant by a secret route grant it to Ziyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zong requested a wax-sealed letter and sent a servant by a secret route to deliver it.

sentences.zh: 縱請為蠟書，令家僮間道賜子儀。

translations.literal: By edict he reviewed the army and was about to depart; Tong-Hua officers, hearing the army rise, then beheaded Zhiguang father and son and sent the heads to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: As Ziyi mustered to march, Tong-Hua officers killed Zhou Zhiguang and his son and sent their heads to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 奉詔大閱軍戎，將發，同華將吏聞軍起，乃斬智光父子，傳首京師。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, Ziyi entered court; chief councilors Yuan Zai and Wang Jin, Vice Director Pei Mian, Jingzhao governor Li Gan, and inner attendant Yu Chao'en together contributed three hundred thousand cash for a banquet at Ziyi's residence; Chao'en gave two hundred bolts of gauze and brocade as the 'head-winding' fee; they parted in utmost joy.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year two, Yuan Zai, Wang Jin, Pei Mian, Li Gan, and Yu Chao'en feasted at Ziyi's mansion, pooling three hundred thousand cash; Yu Chao'en added two hundred bolts of silk as gift money.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，子儀入朝，宰相元載、王縉、僕射裴冕、京兆尹黎幹、內侍魚朝恩共出錢三十萬，置宴於子儀第，恩出羅錦二百匹，為子儀纏頭之費，極歡而罷。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Tibet raided Jingzhou; an edict ordered Ziyi to move thirty thousand infantry and cavalry from Hezhong to encamp at Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Tibet raided Jingzhou; Ziyi was ordered to move thirty thousand troops from Hezhong to Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，吐蕃寇涇州，詔子儀以步騎三萬自河中移屯涇陽。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, the barbarian army withdrew to Lingzhou; he intercepted and defeated them, beheading and capturing twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he intercepted the retreating Tibetans at Lingzhou, taking twenty thousand heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 十月，蕃軍退至靈州，邀擊敗之，斬馘二萬。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, tomb robbers opened the grave of Ziyi's father; the robbers were not captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, robbers violated his father's tomb; none were caught.

sentences.zh: 十二月，盜發子儀父墓，捕盜未獲。

translations.literal: People, because Yu Chao'en had long hated Ziyi, suspected he had sent them.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yu Chao'en hated Ziyi, rumor blamed him for the desecration.

sentences.zh: 人以魚朝恩素惡子儀，疑其使之。

translations.literal: Ziyi in his heart knew the reason; when he was about to enter from Jingyang, discussants feared he would incite mutiny; dukes and ministers worried.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi knew better; as he returned from Jingyang, courtiers feared he might rebel.

sentences.zh: 子儀心知其故，及自涇陽將入，議者慮其構變，公卿憂之。

translations.literal: When Ziyi entered audience, the emperor spoke of it; Ziyi wailed and memorialized, saying, "Your subject long commanded troops and could not forbid violence; soldiers despoiling people's graves—there are indeed many."
translations.idiomatic: At audience the emperor mentioned the tomb; Ziyi wept and said, "I long commanded armies and could not stop violence—my men have robbed many graves."

sentences.zh: 及子儀入見，帝言之，子儀號泣奏曰：「臣久主兵，不能禁暴，軍士殘人之墓，固亦多矣。

translations.literal: This subject's disloyalty and unfiliality received heaven's punishment—it is not a human calamity.
translations.idiomatic: My disloyalty and unfiliality drew heaven's punishment—not men's malice."

sentences.zh: 此臣不忠不孝，上獲天譴，非人患也。

translations.literal: The emperor wept and comforted him, ordering him to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept, consoled him, and sent him back to his command.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷乃安。

translations.literal: The court then was at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the court settle.

sentences.zh: 三年三月，還河中。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year, he returned to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year three he returned to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 八月，吐蕃寇靈武。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Tibet raided Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Tibet attacked Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔子儀率師五萬自河中移鎮奉天。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, an edict ordered Ziyi to lead fifty thousand troops to move from Hezhong to garrison Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was ordered to lead fifty thousand men from Hezhong to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 是月，白元光大破吐蕃靈武。

translations.literal: That month, Bai Yuanguang greatly defeated Tibet at Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: That month Bai Yuanguang routed Tibet at Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 十月，子儀入朝，還鎮河中。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Ziyi entered court and returned to garrison Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he attended court and returned to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 時議以西蕃侵寇，京師不安，馬璘雖在邠州，力不能拒，乃以子儀兼邠寧慶節度，自河中移鎮邠州，徙馬璘為涇原節度使。

translations.literal: At the time discussion held that because western barbarians invaded, the capital was unsettled; though Ma Lin was at Binzhou, his strength could not resist, so Ziyi was made concurrent commissioner of Bin-Ning-Qing circuit, moving from Hezhong to garrison Binzhou, and Ma Lin was transferred to Jingyuan commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: With Tibet pressing the capital and Ma Lin unable to hold Binzhou alone, Ziyi took Bin-Ning-Qing command at Binzhou while Ma Lin moved to Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 八年十月，吐蕃寇涇州，子儀遣先鋒兵馬使渾瑊逆戰於宜祿，不利。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eighth year, Tibet raided Jingzhou; Ziyi sent vanguard army commissioner Hun Jian to meet battle at Yilu—unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight, tenth month, Tibet raided Jingzhou; Hun Jian fought at Yilu and fared badly.

sentences.zh: 會馬璘設伏於潘源，與瑊合擊，大破蕃軍，俘斬數萬計。

translations.literal: When Ma Lin set an ambush at Panyuan and joined with Jian to strike together, they greatly defeated the barbarian army, capturing and beheading tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin ambushed at Panyuan; with Hun Jian he crushed the Tibetans, taking tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 回紇赤心賣馬一萬匹，有司以國計不充，請市千匹。

translations.literal: The Uyghur Chixin offered ten thousand horses for sale; the relevant offices, because state finances were insufficient, asked to buy one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Uyghur Chixin offered ten thousand horses; the treasury could afford only one thousand.

sentences.zh: 子儀以回紇前後立功，不宜阻意，請自納一年奉物，充回紇馬價，雖詔旨不允，內外稱之。

translations.literal: Ziyi, because the Uyghurs had repeatedly established merit, deemed it improper to block their intent, and asked to pay from one year's salary the Uyghur horse price; though the edict did not permit it, inside and outside praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi offered his year's salary to buy the full herd for allies who had served the dynasty; though refused, all praised him.

sentences.zh: 九年，入朝，代宗召對延英。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he entered court; Daizong summoned him for discussion at Yanying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine Daizong received him at Yanying Hall.

sentences.zh: 語及西蕃棄斥，苦戰不暇，言發涕零。

translations.literal: Speaking of western barbarians' rejection and exclusion, bitter fighting without rest, his words ended in streaming tears.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of Tibet's raids and endless war, he wept.

sentences.zh: 既退，復上封論備吐蕃利害，曰：

translations.literal: After retiring, he again submitted a sealed memorial discussing the benefits and harms of guarding against Tibet, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a sealed memorial on defending against Tibet:

sentences.zh: 朔方，國之北門，西禦犬戎，北虞獫狁，五城相去三千餘里。

translations.literal: Shuofang is the state's northern gate, defending against the Dog Rong in the west and the Xianyun in the north; the five cities are three thousand-odd li apart.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang is the northern gate, guarding west against Tibet and north against steppe raiders, with garrisons three thousand li apart.

sentences.zh: 開元、天寶中，戰士十萬，戰馬三萬，才敵一隅。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras, one hundred thousand warriors and thirty thousand war horses barely matched one corner of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaiyuan and Tianbao, a hundred thousand men and thirty thousand horses barely matched one enemy sector.

sentences.zh: 自先皇帝龍飛靈武，戰士從陛下收復兩京，東西南北，曾無寧歲。

translations.literal: Since the late emperor soared to Lingwu, warriors followed Your Majesty to recover the two capitals—east, west, south, and north had never a year of peace.
translations.idiomatic: Since Suzong's rise at Lingwu, the armies that restored the capitals have known no year of peace.

sentences.zh: 中年以仆固之役，又經耗散，人亡三分之二，比於天寶中有十分之一。

translations.literal: Midway through, because of the Pugu campaign, there was again depletion and dispersal; two-thirds of men were lost—compared with Tianbao, one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: The Pugu rebellion cost two-thirds of our strength—one-tenth of Tianbao levels.

sentences.zh: 今吐蕃充斥，勢強十倍，兼河、隴之地，雜羌、渾之眾，每歲來窺近郊。

translations.literal: Now Tibet fills the field, ten times stronger, plus the lands of He and Long with mixed Qiang and Hun masses yearly peering at the near suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet is ten times stronger, and Qiang and Hun in He-Long yearly probe the capital's outskirts.

sentences.zh: 以朔方減十倍之軍，當吐蕃加十倍之騎，欲求制勝，豈易為力！

translations.literal: With Shuofang's army reduced tenfold facing Tibet's cavalry increased tenfold, to seek victory—is it easy to have force!
translations.idiomatic: Tenfold fewer Shuofang troops against tenfold more Tibetan cavalry—victory is hard.

sentences.zh: 入近內地，稱四節度，每將盈萬，每賊兼乘數四。

translations.literal: Entering near the inner lands, they call four circuits; each general exceeds ten thousand, each enemy rider has several mounts.
translations.idiomatic: Near the capital they field four commands of ten thousand each, with multiple mounts per rider.

sentences.zh: 臣所統將士，不當賊四分之一，所有征馬，不當賊百分之二，誠合固守，不宜與戰。

translations.literal: The generals and soldiers I command are not one-fourth of the enemy; the horses we have are not two percent of the enemy's—truly we should hold firm and not suit battle.
translations.idiomatic: My troops are a quarter of theirs, my horses two percent—we must defend, not seek battle.

sentences.zh: 又得馬璘牒，賊擬涉渭而南。

translations.literal: I also received Ma Lin's dispatch: the enemy plans to cross the Wei southward.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Lin reports the enemy may cross the Wei southward.

sentences.zh: 臣若堅壁，恐犯畿甸；

translations.literal: If I hold the walls firmly, I fear they will violate the imperial domain;
translations.idiomatic: If I hold fast, they may strike the capital district;

sentences.zh: 若過畿內，則國人大恐，諸道易搖。

translations.literal: if they pass within the passes, the people will greatly fear and the circuits will easily waver.
translations.idiomatic: if they pass inside, the people will panic and the provinces waver.

sentences.zh: 外有吐蕃之強，中有易搖之眾，外畏內懼，將何以安？

translations.literal: Outside there is Tibet's strength, within the masses easy to shake—fear outside and within—how will we be secure?
translations.idiomatic: Strong enemies without, shaky morale within—how can we be secure?

sentences.zh: 臣伏以陛下橫制勝之術，力非不足，但慮簡練未精，進退未一，時淹師老，地闊勢分。

translations.literal: Your subject reflects that Your Majesty's tactics to overcome by force are not insufficient in strength, but I worry selection and training are not refined, advance and retreat not unified, time delays weary the army, and broad territory scatters force.
translations.idiomatic: Your power is enough, but training, unity, and concentration are lacking.

sentences.zh: 願陛下更詢讜議，慎擇名將，俾之統軍，於諸道各抽精卒，成四五萬，則制勝之道必矣，未可失時。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty further to seek loyal counsel, carefully choose famed generals, have them command armies, and from each circuit draw elite soldiers forming forty or fifty thousand—then the way to victory is fixed; one must not lose the moment.
translations.idiomatic: Choose great generals, concentrate forty or fifty thousand elite troops from every circuit, and victory is assured—do not miss the moment.

sentences.zh: 臣又料河南、河北、山南、江淮小鎮數千，大鎮數萬，空耗月餼，曾不習戰。

translations.literal: Your subject also calculates that Henan, Hebei, Shannan, and Jiang-Huai small garrisons number in thousands, large in tens of thousands, emptyly consuming monthly rations, never practicing war.
translations.idiomatic: Small posts in Henan, Hebei, Shannan, and Jiang-Huai consume rations but never train.

sentences.zh: 臣請抽赴關中，教之戰陣，則軍聲益振，攻守必全，亦長久之計也。

translations.literal: Your subject asks to draw them to Guanzhong and teach battle formations—then the army's prestige will further rise, attack and defense will surely be complete—also a long-term plan.
translations.idiomatic: Bring them to Guanzhong for training—that strengthens attack and defense for the long term.

sentences.zh: 臣猥蒙任遇，垂二十年，今齒發已衰，願避賢路，止足不誡，神明所鑒。

translations.literal: Your subject unworthily received trust and favor for nearly twenty years; now teeth and hair have declined; I wish to yield the path of the worthy; stopping without warning—the spirits witness.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty years of service, I am old and ask to yield to better men—heaven knows my heart.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「卿憂深虛遠，殊沃朕心，始終倚賴，未可執辭也。」

translations.literal: The edict said: "Your worry is deep and your vision far, greatly nourishing Our heart; from first to last We rely on you—you cannot insist on declining."
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "Your counsel nourishes us; we still rely on you—do not resign."

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，詔還朝，攝冢宰，充山陵使，賜號「尚父」，進位太尉、中書令，增實封通計二千戶，給一千五百人糧，二百匹馬草料，所領諸使副元帥並罷。

translations.literal: When Dezong succeeded, an edict recalled him to court; he acted as chief mourner and mausoleum commissioner, was granted the title 'Imperial Father', promoted to Defender-in-Chief and Grand Councilor, actual fief households increased to two thousand in total, given rations for fifteen hundred men and fodder for two hundred horses; the various commissioner and deputy commander posts he led were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong recalled him, made him chief mourner, titled him Imperial Father, promoted him to Defender-in-Chief and grand councilor, doubled his fief, and stripped his military commands.

sentences.zh: 諸子弟女婿拜官者十余人。

translations.literal: Various sons, younger brothers, and sons-in-law receiving appointments numbered more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten sons and sons-in-law received office.

sentences.zh: 建中二年夏，子儀病甚，德宗令舒王誼傳詔省問。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Jianzhong, Ziyi was gravely ill; Dezong had Prince Shu Yi transmit an edict of inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 2, gravely ill, he received an imperial inquiry through Prince Shu Yi.

sentences.zh: 及門，郭氏子弟迎拜於外，王不答拜；

translations.literal: At the gate, the Guo clan sons and younger brothers welcomed and bowed outside; the prince did not return the bow;
translations.idiomatic: At the gate the Guo kin bowed; the prince did not bow in return;

sentences.zh: 子儀臥不能興，以手叩頭謝恩而已。

translations.literal: Ziyi lay ill and could not rise, only knocking his head with his hand to thank grace.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi could not rise and only knocked his head in thanks.

sentences.zh: 六月十四日薨，時年八十五，德宗聞之震悼，廢朝五日，詔曰：

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the sixth month he died, aged eighty-five; Dezong heard and was shocked and grieved, suspending court five days, and edicted:
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth of the sixth month he died at eighty-five; Dezong mourned five days and decreed:

sentences.zh: 天地以四時成物，元首以股肱作輔，公臺之任，鼎足相承，上以調三光，下以蒙五嶽。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth through the four seasons complete things; the sovereign through arms and legs serves as assistants; the duty of duke and minister—the tripod legs mutually sustain—above harmonizing the three luminaries, below covering the five peaks.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven completes the seasons; the ruler relies on ministers as arms and legs to harmonize heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 允釐庶績，鎮撫四夷，體元和之氣，根貞一之德，功至大而不伐，身處高而更安。

translations.literal: Truly ordering the myriad tasks, pacifying and soothing the four barbarians, embodying the qi of primordial harmony, rooted in steadfast unity—merit reaching the greatest yet not boasting, body dwelling high yet more secure.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the realm, pacified barbarians, great in merit yet humble, high in rank yet steady.

sentences.zh: 尚父比呂望之名，為師增周公之位，盛業可久，歿而彌光。

translations.literal: Imperial Father matched the name of Lü Wang; as teacher he added the position of Duke of Zhou—splendid enterprise enduring, death making it brighter.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Father rivaled Lü Wang and Zhou Gong—his glory outlives death.

sentences.zh: 故太尉、兼中書令、上柱國、汾陽郡王、尚父子儀，天降人傑，生知王佐，訓師如子，料敵若神。

translations.literal: The late Defender-in-Chief, concurrent Grand Councilor, Supreme Pillar of State, Prince of Fenyang, Imperial Father Guo Ziyi—heaven dropped a human genius, born knowing kingly assistance, training soldiers like sons, measuring enemies like a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Defender-in-Chief, Grand Councilor, Prince of Fenyang, Imperial Father Guo Ziyi—nature's gift to kings, training men like sons and reading enemies like a god.

sentences.zh: 昔天寶多難，羯胡作禍，鹹秦失險，河洛為戎。

translations.literal: Formerly in Tianbao's many hardships, the Jie barbarians wrought calamity; Xian and Qin lost their passes and He-Luo became Rong.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao's calamity the Jie rebels seized the passes and turned the heartland to war.

sentences.zh: 公能扶翼肅宗，載造區夏。

translations.literal: The Duke could wing and bear Suzong, again creating the Xia domain.
translations.idiomatic: He upheld Suzong and remade the empire.

sentences.zh: 於國有患，勞其戡定；

translations.literal: When the state had calamity, he toiled to pacify and settle it;
translations.idiomatic: When the state was threatened, he pacified it;

sentences.zh: 於邊有寇，藉其驅除。

translations.literal: when the frontier had bandits, it relied on him to drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: when the frontier was raided, he drove the enemy away.

sentences.zh: 安社稷必在於絳侯，定羌戎無逾於充國。

translations.literal: To secure the altars surely lay with the Marquis of Jiang; to settle Qiang and Rong none surpassed Zhao Chongguo.
translations.idiomatic: Like the Marquis of Jiang he saved the state; like Zhao Chongguo he settled the frontier.

sentences.zh: 絳臺綏四散之眾，涇陽降十萬之虜。

translations.literal: At Jiang platform he soothed scattered masses; at Jingyang he reduced a hundred thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiang he rallied scattered troops; at Jingyang he broke a hundred thousand barbarians.

sentences.zh: 勛高今古，名璟夷狄，而勞乎征鎮，二紀於茲。

translations.literal: Merit high in past and present, name shaking the barbarians, yet laboring in campaigns and garrisons—for twenty years here.
translations.idiomatic: His fame shook the steppe through twenty years of campaigns.

sentences.zh: 頃以春秋既高，疆埸多事，罷彼旌鉞，寵在臺衡。

translations.literal: Recently because spring and autumn were already high and the border had many affairs, his banners and axe were removed and favor rested in the platform and balance.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he was relieved of command but honored at court.

sentences.zh: 以公柱石四朝，籓翰萬里，忠貞懸於日月，寵遇冠於人臣，尊其元老，加以崇號，期壽考之永，養勛賢之德。

translations.literal: Because the Duke was pillar and stone through four reigns, screen and rampart for ten thousand li, loyalty suspended from sun and moon, favor and treatment topping all ministers, honoring his senior elder and adding a lofty title, expecting long life, nurturing meritorious virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Pillar of four reigns, loyalty bright as the sun, the court honored his age and merit and wished him long life.

sentences.zh: 膏肓生疾，藥石靡攻，人之雲亡，梁木斯壞。

translations.literal: Sickness entered the vital region; medicine and stone could not attack; man's cloud departed, the beam and ridgepole thus broken.
translations.idiomatic: Illness entered his marrow; medicine failed; the nation's beam broke.

sentences.zh: 雖賻禮加等，輟朝增日，悼之流涕，曷可弭忘！

translations.literal: Though condolence rites were increased and court suspended for added days, grieving until tears flow—how can it be forgotten!
translations.idiomatic: We suspend court and weep—how can we forget!

sentences.zh: 更議追崇，名位斯極，而尊為尚父，官協太師，雖爵秩則同，而體望尤重。

translations.literal: Further deliberation on posthumous elevation—rank and title reach the limit; yet honoring as Imperial Father, office matching Grand Preceptor—though nobility and rank are the same, the stature and expectation are especially heavy.
translations.idiomatic: We elevate him posthumously; Imperial Father and Grand Preceptor exceed ordinary rank.

sentences.zh: 斂以袞冕，旌我元臣。

translations.literal: Enshroud with ceremonial robes and cap—display our chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Let ceremonial robes enshroud our chief minister.

sentences.zh: 聖祖園陵，所宜陪葬，式墓表文終之德，象山追去病之勛。

translations.literal: The sacred ancestor's mausoleum—he should be buried alongside; style the tomb to show the virtue of a final text, image the mountain to chase Huo Qubing's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be buried beside the imperial tomb as befits his final virtue and Huo Qubing's glory.

sentences.zh: 千載如存，九原可作，冊命之禮，有司備焉。

translations.literal: A thousand years as if present, the nine plains can be made—the investiture rites, the relevant offices shall prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Let the rites of investiture be prepared as if he still lived.

sentences.zh: 可贈太師，陪葬建陵。

translations.literal: May posthumously grant Grand Preceptor and burial alongside Jianling.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously grant Grand Preceptor and burial at Jianling.

sentences.zh: 仍令所司備禮冊命，賻絹三千匹、布三千端、米麥三千石。

translations.literal: Still order the relevant offices to prepare rites of investiture; condolence of three thousand bolts of silk, three thousand lengths of cloth, three thousand shi of grain and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Prepare investiture rites and grant three thousand bolts of silk, cloth, and shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 舊令一品墳高丈八，而詔特加十尺。

translations.literal: Formerly the statute for first rank tombs was height one zhang eight chi, but the edict specially added ten chi.
translations.idiomatic: Statute height was one zhang eight chi; the edict added ten chi.

sentences.zh: 群臣以次赴宅吊哭。

translations.literal: Ministers in order went to the residence to mourn and weep.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers came in turn to mourn at his house.

sentences.zh: 兇喪所須，並令官給。

translations.literal: What the violent mourning required was all ordered supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: The state supplied all funeral needs.

sentences.zh: 及葬，上御安福門臨哭送之，百僚陪位隕泣，賜謚曰忠武，配饗代宗廟庭。

translations.literal: At burial, the emperor went to Anfu Gate to face and escort the mourning; hundred officials accompanied weeping; posthumous title Zhongwu, paired sacrifice in Daizong's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong wept at Anfu Gate at the funeral; posthumous name Loyal and Martial, enshrined with Daizong.

sentences.zh: 子曜、旰、晞、昢、晤、曖、曙、映等八人，婿七人，皆朝廷重官。

translations.literal: Sons Yao, Gan, Xi, Pan, Wu, Ai, Shu, Ying—eight men—and seven sons-in-law all held weighty court posts.
translations.idiomatic: Eight sons and seven sons-in-law held high office.

sentences.zh: 諸孫數十人，每群孫問安，不盡辨，頷之而已。

translations.literal: Several tens of grandsons—each time the group of grandsons asked after his health, he could not distinguish them all and only nodded.
translations.idiomatic: With dozens of grandsons he could only nod, unable to name each.

sentences.zh: 參佐官吏六十余人，後位至將相，升朝秩貴位，勒其姓名於石，今在河中府。

translations.literal: Staff and clerks more than sixty, later reaching generals and chiefs, ascending court ranks and noble posts—their names carved on stone, now at Hezhong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty staff later became generals and ministers; their names are carved in stone at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 人士榮之。

translations.literal: Gentlemen and scholars gloried in this.
translations.idiomatic: Men of note took pride in it.

sentences.zh: 史臣裴垍曰：汾陽事上誠藎，臨下寬厚，每降城下邑，所至之處，必得士心。

translations.literal: Historian Pei Ba said: Fenyang served the sovereign with utmost loyalty, treated subordinates with generosity; whenever he descended on a city or town, where he arrived he surely won the gentry's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Historian Pei Ba wrote: Ziyi served with loyalty and ruled subordinates with grace, winning every city he entered.

sentences.zh: 前後遭罹幸臣程元振、魚朝恩譖毀百端，時方握強兵，或方臨戎敵，詔命征之，未嘗不即日應召，故讒謗不能行。

translations.literal: Before and after, favored ministers Cheng Yuanzhen and Yu Chao'en slandered him in a hundred ways; at the time he just held strong troops or faced enemy armies—when edicts summoned him, he never failed to respond the same day, therefore slander could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yuanzhen and Yu Chao'en slandered him endlessly, yet he obeyed every summons the same day, so calumny failed.

sentences.zh: 代宗幸陜時，令以數十騎覘賊，及在涇陽，又陷於胡虜重圍之中，皆以身許國，未嘗以危亡易慮，亦遇天幸，竟免患難。

translations.literal: When Daizong was at Shaan, he ordered him with several tens of horsemen to reconnoiter the enemy; and at Jingyang he again fell within the barbarians' heavy encirclement—both times he pledged his body to the state, never trading worry for danger, also meeting heaven's fortune, finally escaping calamity.
translations.idiomatic: At Shaan and Jingyang he risked his life on reconnaissance and in encirclement, trusting fate and escaping harm.

sentences.zh: 田承嗣方跋扈魏州，傲狠無禮，子儀嘗遣使至，承嗣西望拜之，指其膝謂使者曰：「茲膝不屈於人若干歲矣，今為公拜。

translations.literal: Tian Chengsi was then overbearing at Weizhou, arrogant and ruthless without courtesy; Ziyi once sent an envoy; Chengsi bowed westward and pointed to his knees telling the envoy, "These knees have not bent to anyone for many years; today I bow for the Duke."
translations.idiomatic: Even the arrogant Tian Chengsi bowed to Ziyi's envoy, saying his knees had not bent for years until now.

sentences.zh: 」李靈曜據汴州，公私財賦一皆遏絕，獨子儀封幣經其境，莫敢留之，必持兵衛送。

translations.literal: Li Lingyao held Bianzhou, public and private wealth and grain all cut off; only Ziyi's sealed gifts passing his territory—none dared detain them, necessarily holding troops to escort and send.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lingyao seized all goods at Bianzhou except Ziyi's sealed tribute, which was escorted through untouched.

sentences.zh: 其為豺虎所服如此。

translations.literal: How the wolves and tigers were subdued was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Even predators submitted thus.

sentences.zh: 麾下老將若李懷光輩數十人，皆王侯重貴，子儀頤指進退，如仆隸焉。

translations.literal: Veteran subordinates like Li Huai'guang and several tens of others were all enfeoffed lords and heavy nobles; Ziyi commanded them with chin and finger to advance and retreat as with servants.
translations.idiomatic: Veterans like Li Huai'guang, though princes in rank, obeyed Ziyi like servants.

sentences.zh: 幕府之盛，近代無比。

translations.literal: The staff's splendor—recent ages had no equal.
translations.idiomatic: No staff in recent times matched his.

sentences.zh: 始與李光弼齊名，雖威略不逮，而寬厚得人過之。

translations.literal: At first he was famed equal with Li Guangbi; though martial strategy did not reach him, in generosity winning men he surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: He matched Li Guangbi in fame but surpassed him in winning loyalty.

sentences.zh: 歲入官俸二十四萬貫，私利不在焉。

translations.literal: Annual official salary income two hundred forty thousand strings of cash; private profit was not among it.
translations.idiomatic: His official salary was two hundred forty thousand strings; he took no private cut.

sentences.zh: 其宅在親仁裏，居其裏四分之一，中通永巷，家人三千，相出入者不知其居。

translations.literal: His residence was in Qinren Ward, occupying a quarter of the ward; a lane ran through the middle; household three thousand—those entering and leaving did not know where he lived.
translations.idiomatic: His Qinren Ward mansion filled a quarter of the ward with three thousand household members.

sentences.zh: 前後賜良田美器，名園甲館，聲色珍玩，堆積羨溢，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Before and after, granted fine fields and vessels, famed gardens and leading mansions, sound, color, and precious playthings piled in overflowing abundance beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial gifts of estates, gardens, and treasures overflowed beyond count.

sentences.zh: 代宗不名，呼為大臣。

translations.literal: Daizong did not call his name, addressing him as Great Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong called him Great Minister, not by name.

sentences.zh: 天下以其身為安危者殆二十年。

translations.literal: All under heaven took his person as safety or danger for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: For nearly twenty years the empire's safety rested on him.

sentences.zh: 校中書令考二十有四。

translations.literal: Counted as Grand Councilor twenty-four times.
translations.idiomatic: He served as grand councilor twenty-four times in the rolls.

sentences.zh: 權傾天下而朝不忌，功蓋一代而主不疑，侈窮人欲而君子不之罪。

translations.literal: Power tilted the world yet the court did not envy; merit covered one generation yet the lord did not doubt; extravagance exhausted human desire yet gentlemen did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Power unmatched yet never envied, merit supreme yet never doubted, luxury vast yet never condemned.

sentences.zh: 富貴壽考，繁衍安泰，哀榮終始，人道之盛，此無缺焉。

translations.literal: Wealth, nobility, long life, and peace, prosperity and ease, sorrow and glory from start to finish—the fullness of the human way, in this nothing is lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth, honor, long life, and a glorious end—human fortune found no fuller example.

sentences.zh: 唯以讒怒，誣奏判官戶部郎中張譚杖殺之，物議為薄。

translations.literal: Only because of slander's anger, he falsely memorialized and had his judge of accounts Zhang Tan beaten to death—the opinion of the masses deemed this shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Only when angered by slander he had judge Zhang Tan beaten to death—critics judged that petty.

sentences.zh: 曜，子儀長子。

translations.literal: Yao was Ziyi's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was Ziyi's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 性孝友廉謹。

translations.literal: By nature filial, friendly, honest, and careful.
translations.idiomatic: He was filial, friendly, honest, and careful.

sentences.zh: 子儀薨，出征於外，留曜治家，少長千人，皆得其所。

translations.literal: When Ziyi died, campaigning abroad, he left Yao to manage the house; old and young a thousand—all obtained their place.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyi died on campaign, Yao ran the household of a thousand kin fairly.

sentences.zh: 諸弟爭飾池館，盛其車服，曜以儉樸自處。

translations.literal: Younger brothers competed to adorn pools and halls and magnify carriage and dress; Yao kept himself frugal and plain.
translations.idiomatic: Brothers flaunted wealth; Yao lived plainly.

sentences.zh: 累遷至太子賓客。

translations.literal: He successively rose to Crown Prince's Guest.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to crown prince's guest.

sentences.zh: 建中初，子儀罷兵柄，乃遍加諸子官，以曜為太子少保。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianzhong, when Ziyi lost military power, he broadly added offices to the sons, making Yao Crown Prince's Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When Ziyi lost command, Yao became crown prince's junior mentor.

sentences.zh: 子儀曜遵遺命，四朝所賜名馬珍玩，悉皆上獻，德宗復賜之，曜乃散諸昆弟。

translations.literal: Ziyi and Yao followed the testament: famous horses and precious playthings granted by the four reigns were all presented above; Dezong returned them, and Yao then distributed them among the brothers.
translations.idiomatic: They surrendered imperial gifts per Ziyi's will; Dezong returned them and Yao shared them among kin.

sentences.zh: 子儀薨後，楊炎、盧杞相次秉政，奸諂用事，尤忌勛族。

translations.literal: After Ziyi's death, Yang Yan and Lu Qi successively held power; wicked flatterers handled affairs, especially jealous of meritorious clans.
translations.idiomatic: After Ziyi's death Yang Yan and Lu Qi persecuted great clans.

sentences.zh: 子儀之婿太仆卿趙縱、少府少監李洞清、光祿卿王宰，皆以有人告訐細過，相次貶黜。

translations.literal: Ziyi's sons-in-law Grand Master of the Imperial Stud Zhao Zong, Vice Director of the Palace Workshops Li Dongqing, and Minister of Imperial Sacrifices Wang Zai—all because someone informed on minor faults were in succession demoted and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Sons-in-law Zhao Zong, Li Dongqing, and Wang Zai were demoted on petty denunciations.

sentences.zh: 曜家大恐，賴宰相張鎰力為庇護。

translations.literal: Yao's household was greatly afraid, relying on chief councilor Zhang Yi to exert strength in shelter.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's family feared ruin until Zhang Yi protected them.

sentences.zh: 奸人幸其危懼，多論奪田宅奴婢，曜不敢訴。

translations.literal: Wicked men, rejoicing in their peril and fear, mostly argued to seize fields, houses, and slaves; Yao did not dare complain.
translations.idiomatic: Predators seized their property while Yao dared not protest.

sentences.zh: 德宗微知之，詔曰：「尚父子儀，有大勛力，保乂皇家，嘗誓以山河，琢之金石，十世之宥，其可忘也！

translations.literal: Dezong slightly knew this and edicted: "Imperial Father Guo Ziyi had great merit and strength, preserving and comforting the royal house; he once swore on mountains and rivers, carved on metal and stone—a pardon for ten generations—how can it be forgotten!
translations.idiomatic: Dezong decreed: "Imperial Father Ziyi's ten-generation pardon must not be forgotten!

sentences.zh: 其家前時與人為市，以子儀身歿，名被誣構，欲論奪之，有司無得為理。

translations.literal: His household's earlier dealings with others in market—because Ziyi's person had died, names were falsely framed, wanting to argue and seize—relevant offices must not entertain the case.
translations.idiomatic: No official may seize Guo property by false claims after Ziyi's death.

sentences.zh: 」詔下方已。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued below, it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was promulgated, the seizures stopped.

sentences.zh: 曜居喪得禮，若儒家子，服未闋寢疾，或勸其茹蔥薤，曜竟不屬口。

translations.literal: Yao observed mourning with proper rites like a Confucian son; before mourning ended he took to bed with illness; some urged him to eat scallions and leeks; Yao ultimately did not put them to mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Yao mourned by Confucian rites; ill before mourning ended, he refused even scallions and leeks.

sentences.zh: 建中四年三月卒，贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year of Jianzhong he died; posthumously granted Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 4, third month, he died and was posthumously made grand mentor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 晞，子儀第三子。

translations.literal: Xi was Ziyi's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was Ziyi's third son.

sentences.zh: 少善騎射，常從父征伐。

translations.literal: In youth he was skilled at horsemanship and archery and often followed his father on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he excelled at riding and archery and campaigned with his father.

sentences.zh: 初以戰功授左贊善大夫，從廣平王收復兩京，晞力戰於香積寺、陜西，皆出奇兵克捷，以功加銀青光祿大夫、鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: At first for battle merit he was made Left Supporter of Goodness Grand Master; following the Prince of Guangping in recovering the two capitals, Xi fought hard at Xiangji Temple and west of Shaan, both times sending surprise troops to victory; for merit added Silver and Blue Light Grand Master of the Imperial Household and Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He earned office at Xiangji and Shaan under the Prince of Guangping with daring surprise attacks.

sentences.zh: 後河中軍亂，殺節度使李國貞、荔非元禮於絳，詔以子儀為河東關內副元帥，鎮絳州，時四方擾叛，多逐戎帥，子儀至絳，誅其元惡，其黨頗不自安，欲謀翻變。

translations.literal: Later the Hezhong army mutinied, killing military commissioners Li Guozhen and Lifei Yuanli at Jiang; an edict made Ziyi Hedong-Guannei deputy commander-in-chief, garrisoning Jiangzhou; at the time the four directions were disturbed in rebellion, many driving out military commissioners; when Ziyi reached Jiang he executed the chief villains; their faction was quite unsettled and plotted mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: After mutineers killed commanders at Jiang, Ziyi executed ringleaders but their faction plotted revolt.

sentences.zh: 晞知其謀，選親兵四千，伏甲以防之，常持弓警夜，不寐者凡七十日，叛將竟不敢發，以功拜殿中監。

translations.literal: Xi learned their plot, chose four thousand trusted troops, hid armor to guard against it, often holding bow on night watch—for seventy days without sleep; the rebel generals ultimately did not dare act; for merit he was made Palace Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Xi learned of the plot, kept four thousand guards alert seventy nights, and earned palace supervisor.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年，仆固懷恩誘吐蕃、回紇入寇。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangde, Pugu Huai'en incited Tibet and Uyghurs to invade.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangde 2, Huai'en stirred Tibet and Uyghurs to invade.

sentences.zh: 加晞御史中丞，領朔方軍以援邠州，與馬璘合勢，大破蕃軍。

translations.literal: Xi was added Censor-in-Chief, leading Shuofang army to aid Binzhou; with Ma Lin combining strength, they greatly defeated the barbarian army.
translations.idiomatic: Made censor-in-chief, he led Shuofang to Binzhou and with Ma Lin crushed the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，懷恩誘虜再寇邠州，陣於涇北，子儀令晞率步卒五千、騎軍五百，出西南掩擊之。

translations.literal: That winter Huai'en incited barbarians again to raid Binzhou, forming battle lines north of Jing; Ziyi ordered Xi to lead five thousand foot and five hundred cavalry to strike from the southwest in concealment.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Xi led five thousand foot and five hundred horse in a concealed strike north of Jing.

sentences.zh: 晞以兵寡不敵，持而不戰，及至晡晚，乘其半濟而擊之，大破獯虜，斬首五千級。

translations.literal: Xi because troops were few and could not match the enemy, held and did not fight; when evening came, riding their half-crossing he struck and greatly defeated the Hun barbarians, beheading five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, he waited until dusk and struck the enemy half across the river, taking five thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 是時連戰皆捷，詔加御史大夫，子儀固讓不受。

translations.literal: At that time successive battles were all victorious; an edict added Censor-in-Chief; Ziyi firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: After successive victories an edict promoted him; Ziyi refused the honor for him.

sentences.zh: 永泰二年，檢校左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongtai, made Acting Left Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongtai 2 he became acting left regular palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 大歷七年，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dali, added Grand General with the Honorific Acting Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 7 he received grand general with honorific acting grand master.

sentences.zh: 十二年，丁母憂；

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he entered mourning for his mother;
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve he mourned his mother;

sentences.zh: 服除，加檢校工部尚書，判秘書省事。

translations.literal: when mourning ended, added Acting Minister of Works, judging Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: after mourning he became acting minister of works overseeing the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，丁父喪，持服京城。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, he entered mourning for his father, observing mourning in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 2 he mourned his father in the capital.

sentences.zh: 硃泚構逆，遣人就第問訊，欲令掌兵，晞佯瘖，噤口不言，泚以兵脅之，晞終不語，賊知其不可用，乃止。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci rebelled, sent someone to his residence to inquire, wishing to have him command troops; Xi feigned muteness, sealed mouth and did not speak; Ci used troops to coerce him; Xi ultimately did not speak; the rebels knew he was unusable and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci coerced him to command, Xi feigned muteness until the rebels gave up.

sentences.zh: 晞潛奔奉天，僅而獲免。

translations.literal: Xi secretly fled to Fengtian and barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He fled secretly to Fengtian and barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 初，晞兄曜襲父代國公，實封二千戶，及曜卒，詔曰：「故尚父、太尉中書令、汾陽王，功格上玄，道光下土，積其善慶，垂裕無窮。

translations.literal: At first Xi's elder brother Yao inherited the father's Duke of Dai, actual fief two thousand households; when Yao died, the edict said: "The late Imperial Father, Defender-in-Chief, Grand Councilor, Prince of Fenyang—merit reaching upper mystery, the Way's light covering lower earth—accumulated good fortune, extending abundance without end.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao died, the throne recalled Ziyi's merit and the survival of the clan.

sentences.zh: 雖嫡長雲殂，支宗斯盛，汾陽舊邑，盍有丕承。

translations.literal: Though the direct eldest passed like a cloud, the branch clan is thus flourishing; the old seat of Fenyang—how can there fail to be grand succession?
translations.idiomatic: Though the eldest line ended, the branch flourishes to inherit Fenyang.

sentences.zh: 其男前左散騎常侍、駙馬都尉、食實封五百戶曖，夙稟義方，居忠履孝，儷崇銀榜，攄美金章，繼撫先封，允宜聽復。

translations.literal: His son the former Left Regular Palace Attendant, Commandant of the Horse, actual fief five hundred households Ai—inherited righteousness's method, dwelling in loyalty and treading filial piety, paired in honored silver tablet, displaying golden seal, continuing to soothe the prior enfeoffment—properly should be heard to resume.
translations.idiomatic: Ai, horse commandant with five hundred households, should resume the fief for loyalty and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 曖兄檢校工部尚書、守太子賓客、趙國公晞，並弟右金吾將軍、祁國公、食實封二百五十戶曙，太子左諭德映等，並休有令名，保其先業，宜允推恩之典，以明延嗣之誠。

translations.literal: Ai's elder brother Acting Minister of Works, Guardian of the Crown Prince, Duke of Zhao Xi, and younger brother Right Golden Guard General, Duke of Qi, actual fief two hundred fifty households Shu, Crown Prince's Left Mentor Ying, and others—all rest in fine names, preserving their prior enterprise; properly should grant the canon of extended grace to clarify the sincerity of continued succession.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, Shu, Ying, and others should share the extended grace of succession.

sentences.zh: 其實封二千戶，宜準式減半，余可分襲。

translations.literal: The actual fief of two thousand households should by statute be halved; the remainder may be divided in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The two-thousand-household fief should be halved by statute and divided.

sentences.zh: 曖可襲代國公，仍通前襲三百戶；

translations.literal: Ai may succeed to Duke of Dai, still combining prior succession three hundred households;
translations.idiomatic: Ai may inherit Duke of Dai with three hundred prior households;

sentences.zh: 晞可二百五十戶；

translations.literal: Xi may have two hundred fifty households;
translations.idiomatic: Xi two hundred fifty;

sentences.zh: 曙可五十戶，通前三百七十戶；

translations.literal: Shu may have fifty households, combining prior three hundred seventy;
translations.idiomatic: Shu fifty plus three hundred seventy prior;

sentences.zh: 映可二百三十五戶。

translations.literal: Ying may have two hundred thirty-five households.
translations.idiomatic: Ying two hundred thirty-five.

sentences.zh: 」尋又詔尚父子儀男晞、曖、映、曙四人所襲實封，各減五十戶，以賜郭曜男鉾、郭晤男鐇，各襲一百戶。

translations.literal: Soon again an edict: the actual fiefs inherited by Imperial Father Guo Ziyi's sons Xi, Ai, Ying, and Shu—each reduced fifty households, granted to Guo Yao's son Mou and Guo Wu's son Feng, each succeeding one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Later each son's fief was reduced fifty households for Yao's and Wu's grandsons.

sentences.zh: 晞至行在，復檢校工部尚書、太子詹事；

translations.literal: Xi reached the imperial camp, again Acting Minister of Works, Crown Prince's Household Administrator;
translations.idiomatic: Xi rejoined the court as acting minister of works and crown prince's household administrator;

sentences.zh: 從駕還京，改太子賓客。

translations.literal: following the carriage back to the capital, changed to Crown Prince's Guest.
translations.idiomatic: then became crown prince's guest after the return.

sentences.zh: 晞子鋼為朔方節度使杜希全賓佐，希全以鋼攝豐州刺史。

translations.literal: Xi's son Gang was staff to Shuofang commissioner Du Xiquan; Xiquan had Gang act as Fengzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's son Gang served Shuofang commissioner Du Xiquan as acting Fengzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 晞以鋼幼弱，恐不任邊職，貞元七年，晞上章請罷鋼官。

translations.literal: Xi because Gang was young and weak, feared he could not bear frontier duty; in the seventh year of Zhengyuan, Xi memorialized asking to remove Gang's office.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengyuan 7 Xi asked to remove young Gang from frontier office.

sentences.zh: 德宗遣中使召之，鋼疑以他事見攝，乃單騎走入吐蕃。

translations.literal: Dezong sent a palace envoy to summon him; Gang suspected he was summoned for another matter and alone on horseback fled into Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned by imperial envoy, Gang fled alone into Tibet.

sentences.zh: 蕃將見鋼獨叛，不納，置之筏上，流入黃河令歸，杜希全得之，送赴京師，賜鋼自盡，晞亦坐子免官。

translations.literal: The Tibetan general, seeing Gang alone defect, did not accept him, placed him on a raft, floated him into the Yellow River to send him back; Du Xiquan got him, sent him to the capital; Gang was granted suicide; Xi also lost office because of his son.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet sent him back on a raft; the court ordered Gang to kill himself and removed Xi.

sentences.zh: 明年，復授太子賓客。

translations.literal: The next year, again appointed Crown Prince's Guest.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he was again crown prince's guest.

sentences.zh: 貞元十年卒，贈兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhengyuan he died; posthumously granted Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengyuan 10 he died, posthumously minister of war.

sentences.zh: 晞次子鈞。

translations.literal: Xi's second son Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's second son was Jun.

sentences.zh: 鈞子承嘏別有傳。

translations.literal: Jun's son Chengjia has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Jung's son Chengjia has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 曖，子儀第六子。

translations.literal: Ai was Ziyi's sixth son.
translations.idiomatic: Ai was Ziyi's sixth son.

sentences.zh: 年十余歲，尚代宗第四女升平公主，時升平年亦與暖相類。

translations.literal: Aged just over ten, he married Emperor Daizong's fourth daughter Princess Shengping; at the time Shengping's age also matched Ai's.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he married Daizong's daughter Princess Shengping, near his own age.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，恩寵冠於戚裏，歲時錫賚珍玩，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, favor surpassed the imperial kin; yearly grants of precious playthings beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dali era imperial favor and gifts were unmatched among kin.

sentences.zh: 大歷十三年，有詔毀除白渠水支流碾硙，以妨民溉田。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Dali, an edict ordered destruction of Baiqu Canal's branch watermills that hindered irrigation for the people.
translations.idiomatic: In Dali 13 an edict abolished branch canal mills that blocked irrigation.

sentences.zh: 升平有脂粉硙兩輪，郭子儀私硙兩輪，所司未敢毀徹。

translations.literal: Shengping had two cosmetic mills; Guo Ziyi privately had two mills; the relevant offices did not dare destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Shengping and Ziyi each kept two mills until officials dared not touch them.

sentences.zh: 公主見代宗訴之，帝謂公主曰：「吾行此詔，蓋為蒼生，爾豈不識我意耶？

translations.literal: The princess saw Daizong to complain; the emperor told the princess, "I issue this edict for the common people—do you not recognize my intent?
translations.idiomatic: The princess complained; Daizong said the edict was for the people—she should lead by example.

sentences.zh: 可為眾率先。

translations.literal: You can take the lead for the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: Take the lead for all."

sentences.zh: 」公主即日命毀。

translations.literal: The princess that day ordered destruction.
translations.idiomatic: She destroyed her mills that same day.

sentences.zh: 由是勢門碾硙八十余所，皆毀之。

translations.literal: Thereupon eighty-odd mills of powerful families were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Then eighty powerful families' mills were torn down.

sentences.zh: 曖檢校左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Ai was made Acting Left Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Ai became acting left regular palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 建中末，公主坐事，留之禁中，曖亦不令出入。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianzhong, the princess because of an affair was detained in the palace; Ai also was not allowed in or out.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jianzhong the princess was confined and Ai was locked out with her.

sentences.zh: 既而硃泚之亂，不知車駕幸奉天，為賊所逼，欲授偽官，曖辭以居喪被疾。

translations.literal: Soon Zhu Ci's rebellion—they did not know the imperial carriage had gone to Fengtian; forced by rebels, wishing to grant false office, Ai declined citing mourning illness.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhu Ci's revolt, Ai refused puppet office citing mourning illness.

sentences.zh: 既而與兄晞、弟曙及升平公主皆奔奉天，德宗喜，並釋前咎，待之如初，復銀青光祿大夫、檢校左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon with elder brother Xi, younger brother Shu, and Princess Shengping all fled to Fengtian; Dezong rejoiced, all released prior faults, treated as at first, restored Silver and Blue Light Grand Master, Acting Left Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He fled with Xi, Shu, and Shengping to Fengtian; Dezong pardoned them and restored honors.

sentences.zh: 從駕至山南，改太常卿同正員。

translations.literal: Following the carriage to Shannan, changed to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices with concurrent validity.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the court to Shannan as minister of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 貞元中，帝為皇孫廣陵郡王納曖女為妃。

translations.literal: In the Zhengyuan era, the emperor for the imperial grandson Prince of Guangling took Ai's daughter as consort.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengyuan the emperor married Ai's daughter to Prince of Guangling.

sentences.zh: 曖，貞元十六年七月卒，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Ai died in the seventh month of the sixteenth year of Zhengyuan; posthumously granted Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ai died in Zhengyuan 16, seventh month, posthumously left vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 升平公主，元和五年十月薨，贈虢國大長公主，謚曰懿。

translations.literal: Princess Shengping died in the tenth month of the fifth year of Yuanhe; posthumously granted Grand Princess of Guo, posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Shengping died in Yuanhe 5, posthumously Grand Princess of Guo, posthumous Yi.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王即位，為憲宗皇帝，妃生穆宗皇帝。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangling succeeded as Emperor Xianzong; the consort bore Emperor Muzong.
translations.idiomatic: Their daughter became empress to Xianzong and mother of Muzong.

sentences.zh: 元和十五年，穆宗即位，尊郭妃為皇太后，詔曰：「追遠飾終，先王令典。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Yuanhe, Muzong succeeded; he honored Consort Guo as Empress Dowager, edicting: "Pursuing the distant and adorning the end—the former kings' standard canon.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 15 Muzong honored her as empress dowager, citing ancient rites.

sentences.zh: 況積仁累義，事已顯於身前；

translations.literal: Moreover accumulated benevolence and accumulated righteousness—the matter already displayed before the body;
translations.idiomatic: Her accumulated virtue was plain in life;

sentences.zh: 祥會慶傳，福遂流於天下。

translations.literal: auspicious meetings and celebratory transmission—fortune then flowed through all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: her blessings spread through the realm.

sentences.zh: 式光盛德，爰舉徽章，尊尊親親，於是乎在。

translations.literal: Thus displaying splendid virtue, therefore raising the emblem badge—honoring the honored and cherishing the kin—herein lies.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the court raised her honors and cherished kin.

sentences.zh: 皇太后父贈尚書左僕射曖，克荷崇構，有勞王家，孝友本於生知，英華發於事任，實修一德，歷仕三朝。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager's father posthumously granted Left Vice Director Ai—could bear lofty structure, had toil for the royal house; filial piety and friendship rooted in inborn knowledge, brilliance issuing from office and trust; truly cultivated one virtue, successively serving three courts.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Ai served three reigns with filial loyalty and talent.

sentences.zh: 建中末年，屬有大難，畢力扈駕，忘軀即戎，忠貞之節，國史明備。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianzhong, there was great calamity; exerting strength escorting the carriage, forgetting body entering battle—loyal fidelity's integrity, the state history clearly complete.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong's crisis he escorted the emperor at risk of life—history records his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 才高望洽，是膺沁水之祥；

translations.literal: Talent high and renown harmonized—therefore received Qinshui's auspice;
translations.idiomatic: His talent won Qinshui's blessing;

sentences.zh: 德厚流光，乃啟塗山之祚。

translations.literal: virtue thick, light flowing—thus opened Tushan's enthronement.
translations.idiomatic: his virtue opened Tushan's succession.

sentences.zh: 肆予小子，獲纘大業，未展定申之命，敢緣褒紀之恩，俾繼維師，用不縟禮。

translations.literal: I your young son obtained continuing the great enterprise; not yet displaying the orders of ding and shen—I dare follow the canon of praise and record, causing continuation of the maintaining master, using not thick rites.
translations.idiomatic: I, Muzong, extend grace though full rites are not yet due.

sentences.zh: 可贈太傅。

translations.literal: May posthumously grant Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously grant him Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 」曖子釗、鏦、銛。

translations.literal: Ai's sons Zhao, Cong, and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Ai's sons were Zhao, Cong, and Xian.

sentences.zh: 曙，代宗朝累歷司農卿，居父憂。

translations.literal: Shu, in Daizong's court successively served as Minister of Imperial Granaries, dwelling in mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: Shu served as minister of imperial granaries under Daizong and mourned his father.

sentences.zh: 建中三年冬，舒王誼為淮西、山南諸大元帥，以曙檢校左庶子，為元帥府都押牙。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Jianzhong, Prince Shu Yi was supreme commander of Huai-Xi and Shannan circuits; Shu was made Acting Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent, chief adjutant of the commander-in-chief's staff.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 3 winter Shu served Prince Shu Yi as chief adjutant.

sentences.zh: 京城亂，從幸山南，轉太府卿。

translations.literal: Capital chaos—followed fortune to Shannan, transferred to Minister of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In capital chaos he followed the court to Shannan as minister of the treasury.

sentences.zh: 隨駕還京，拜左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Following the carriage back to the capital, made Left Golden Guard General-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Chang'an, he became left golden guard general.

sentences.zh: 貞元末卒。

translations.literal: Died at the end of Zhengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the end of Zhengyuan.

sentences.zh: 釗，偉姿儀，身長七尺，方口豐下，沈默寡言。

translations.literal: Zhao—majestic bearing, body seven chi tall, square mouth and full jaw, silent and sparing of words.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was tall and handsome, seven feet, silent and grave.

sentences.zh: 母升平長公主。

translations.literal: Mother was Princess Shengping the Long Princess.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Princess Shengping.

sentences.zh: 代宗朝，釗為外孫，恩寵逾等，起家為太常寺奉禮郎。

translations.literal: In Daizong's court, as maternal grandson favor exceeded rank; began office as Director of Ceremonies in the Grand Imperial Sacrifices Office.
translations.idiomatic: As Daizong's grandson he entered the Grand Sacrifices Office.

sentences.zh: 德宗朝，累官至太子右庶子。

translations.literal: In Dezong's court, successively reached Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dezong he rose to right guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 元和初，為左金吾衛大將軍，充左街使。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanhe, was Left Golden Guard General-in-Chief, filling Left Street Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe he became left golden guard general and left street commissioner.

sentences.zh: 九年十一月，檢校工部尚書，兼邠州刺史，充邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the ninth year, Acting Minister of Works, concurrently Binzhou prefect, Binning military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 9, eleventh month, he became acting minister of works and Binning commissioner.

sentences.zh: 數歲，檢校戶部尚書，入為司農卿。

translations.literal: After several years, Acting Minister of Revenue, entered as Minister of Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: After years as revenue minister he became minister of imperial granaries.

sentences.zh: 釗，大勛之後，姻聯戚裏，而謙和接物，恭慎自持，居家臨民，無驕怠之色，無奢侈之失，士君子重之。

translations.literal: Zhao, descendant of great merit, marriage-linked imperial kin, yet humble in receiving others, respectful and cautious in self-restraint, dwelling at home facing the people without arrogant slack color, without extravagant fault—gentlemen and scholars esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Despite imperial connections, Zhao was humble and esteemed by scholars.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月，憲宗寢疾彌旬，諸中貴人秉權者欲議廢立，紛紛未定。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year, Xianzong's illness lasted more than ten days; various inner powerful eunuchs holding power wished to discuss deposing and enthroning—confusion unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 15 Xianzong fell ill and eunuchs debated succession.

sentences.zh: 穆宗在東宮，心甚憂之，遣人問計於釗，釗曰：「殿下身為皇太子，但旦夕視膳，謹守以俟，又何慮乎！

translations.literal: Muzong in the Eastern Palace was deeply worried, sent someone to ask Zhao's plan; Zhao said, "Your Highness as crown prince—only morning and evening attend meals, carefully guard and wait—what worry again!"
translations.idiomatic: Muzong asked his counsel; Zhao said a crown prince need only attend the emperor and wait.

sentences.zh: 」迄今稱釗得元舅之體。

translations.literal: To this day they say Zhao obtained the proper body of maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: He is praised as the model imperial uncle.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，冊皇太后南內，推崇外氏，以釗兼司農卿。

translations.literal: When Muzong succeeded, invested the Empress Dowager in the Southern Inner Palace, exalted the maternal kin, making Zhao concurrent Minister of Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong made Zhao concurrent minister of imperial granaries.

sentences.zh: 未幾，檢校戶部尚書，充河陽三城懷節度使。

translations.literal: Before long, Acting Minister of Revenue, filling Heyang Three Cities Huai military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was revenue minister and Heyang commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歲中，換河中尹、河中晉絳慈隰節度使。

translations.literal: Mid-year, exchanged to Heyang metropolitan governor, Heyang-Jin-Jiang-Ci-Li military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-year he became Heyang governor and military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 釗歷踐籓鎮，以汾陽胄胤，材能選用，不獨憑椒房之勢，所蒞簡約不撓，其俗自理。

translations.literal: Zhao successively tread frontier commands; as Fenyang descendant, talent and ability selected for use—not solely relying on empress kin power; where he arrived was simple and unyielding, its customs self-ordered.
translations.idiomatic: As Ziyi's heir he governed frontiers by ability, not only by kinship, and order followed.

sentences.zh: 敬宗即位，尊郭太后為太皇太后，征釗為兵部尚書，兼檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: When Jingzong succeeded, honored Empress Dowager Guo as Grand Empress Dowager, summoned Zhao as Minister of War, concurrently Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong summoned him as minister of war and acting left vice director.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為梓州刺史、劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: The next year, sent out as Zizhou prefect, Jiannan East Circuit military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he went out as Jiannan East commissioner.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，加司空。

translations.literal: When Wenzong succeeded, added Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong added minister of works.

sentences.zh: 大和三年冬，南蠻陷巂州，遂寇西川，杜元穎失於控禦，蠻軍陷成都府外城。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Taihe, southern barbarians took Qiongzhou, then raided western Sichuan; Du Yuanying failed in control; barbarian army took Chengdu's outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 3 winter Nanzhao took Qiongzhou and breached Chengdu's outer wall.

sentences.zh: 朝廷未暇除帥，乃以釗兼領西川節度。

translations.literal: The court had no leisure to appoint a commander; thus made Zhao concurrently lead western Sichuan command.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Zhao concurrent western Sichuan commander.

sentences.zh: 蠻軍已寇樟州，諸道援軍未至，川軍寡弱，不可令戰。

translations.literal: Barbarian army already raided Zhangzhou; relief armies from circuits had not arrived; Sichuan troops few and weak—could not order battle.
translations.idiomatic: With relief late and Sichuan weak, battle was impossible.

sentences.zh: 釗致書於蠻首領泬巔，責以侵寇之意，泬巔曰：「杜元穎不守疆埸，屢侵吾圉，以是修報也。

translations.literal: Zhao sent letter to barbarian chieftain Ju Dian, reproaching the meaning of invasion; Ju Dian said, "Du Yuanying did not guard the border, repeatedly encroaching on our lands—therefore this repayment."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao rebuked chieftain Ju Dian, who blamed Du Yuanying's border failures.

sentences.zh: 」與釗修好而退。

translations.literal: With Zhao renewed friendship and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They renewed friendship and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉之，授成都尹、劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: The court praised this, granted Chengdu metropolitan governor, Jiannan West Circuit military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised him and made him Chengdu governor and western Sichuan commissioner.

sentences.zh: 與南詔立約，疆陲不擾。

translations.literal: With Nanzhao established treaty, the border was not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: He treaty with Nanzhao and kept the border quiet.

sentences.zh: 以疾求代。

translations.literal: Because of illness asked to be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he asked to be replaced.

sentences.zh: 四年，入為太常卿、檢校司徒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, entered as Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, Acting Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he became minister of imperial sacrifices and acting minister of education.

sentences.zh: 十二月，在道卒，詔贈司徒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, died on the road; edict posthumously granted Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he died on the road, posthumously minister of education.

sentences.zh: 子仲文、仲辭。

translations.literal: Sons Zhongwen and Zhongci.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhongwen and Zhongci.

sentences.zh: 仲文，大和末為殿中少監。

translations.literal: Zhongwen, at the end of Taihe, was Vice Supervisor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Taihe, Zhongwen was vice supervisor of the palace.

sentences.zh: 開成初，詔仲文襲父太原郡公，制上，給事中封敕奏曰：「伏準制書，贈司徒郭釗嫡男仲文襲封太原郡公者，臣近訪知郭釗妻沈氏，公主之女，代宗皇帝外孫，有男仲辭，已選尚主。
