translations.literal: At the start of Kaicheng, an edict had Zhongwen succeed to his father's Duke of Taiyuan; when the regulation was submitted, Supervising Secretary Feng Chi memorialized: "According to the regulation text, posthumously granted Minister of Education Guo Zhao's legitimate son Zhongwen succeeding to Duke of Taiyuan—your subject recently inquired and learned Guo Zhao's wife Lady Shen, the princess's daughter, Emperor Daizong's maternal grandson, has a son Zhongci already selected to marry a princess.
translations.idiomatic: At Kaicheng's start, Feng Chi challenged Zhongwen's succession, noting Zhao's wife Lady Shen had son Zhongci already chosen to marry a princess.

sentences.zh: 仲文不合假冒，自稱嫡子。

translations.literal: Zhongwen is not fit to falsely claim, calling himself legitimate son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen falsely claimed to be the legitimate heir.

sentences.zh: 若仲文承嫡，即沈氏須黜居別室，仲辭不合配尚貴主。

translations.literal: If Zhongci succeeds as legitimate, then Lady Shen must be dismissed to a separate chamber; Zhongci is not fit to be matched to an honored princess.
translations.idiomatic: If Zhongwen were legitimate, Lady Shen would be set aside and Zhongci could not marry a princess.

sentences.zh: 伏以郭仲文，尚父子儀之孫，太皇太后之侄，戚裏勛門，無與儔比，婚姻嫡庶，朝野具知，奪宗之配，實玷風教。

translations.literal: Your subject reflects that Guo Zhongwen is Imperial Father Guo Ziyi's grandson, the Grand Empress Dowager's nephew—imperial kin and meritorious gate, none comparable; marriage legitimate and secondary—the court and wilds all know; seizing the succession's match truly stains wind and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: As Ziyi's grandson and the empress dowager's nephew, Zhongwen's false claim stained propriety known to all.

sentences.zh: 且仲文、仲辭既非同出，襲封尚主，不可並行。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhongwen and Zhongci are not from the same birth; succeeding enfeoffment and marrying a princess cannot both proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Succession and imperial marriage could not both go to conflicting claims.

sentences.zh: 伏請付臺勘當。

translations.literal: Your subject asks that it be sent to the censorate for investigation."
translations.idiomatic: He asked the censorate to investigate.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「以萬年縣尉仲辭襲封。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Let Wanian district defender Zhongci succeed to the enfeoffment."
translations.idiomatic: The edict awarded succession to Wanian defender Zhongci.

sentences.zh: 」仲文落下，以太皇太后侄，不之罪。

translations.literal: Zhongwen was removed from office; because he was the Grand Empress Dowager's nephew, he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen lost office but escaped punishment as the empress dowager's nephew.

sentences.zh: 尋以仲辭為銀青光祿大夫、檢校中少監、駙馬都尉，襲封太原郡公，尚饒陽公主。

translations.literal: Soon Zhongci was made Silver and Blue Light Grand Master, Acting Vice Supervisor of the Palace, Commandant of the Horse, succeeding to Duke of Taiyuan, marrying Princess Raoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongci became horse commandant, Duke of Taiyuan, and married Princess Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 又仲辭兄詹事府丞仲恭，為銀青光祿大夫，尚金堂公主。

translations.literal: Also Zhongci's elder brother Crown Prince's Household Registrar Zhonggong was Silver and Blue Light Grand Master, marrying Princess Jintang.
translations.idiomatic: Brother Zhonggong married Princess Jintang.

sentences.zh: 幼明，尚父子儀之母弟也。

translations.literal: Youming was Imperial Father Guo Ziyi's mother's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Youming was Ziyi's maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 性謹願無過，不工武藝，喜賓客飲宴，居家禦眾，皆得其歡心。

translations.literal: By nature cautious and obedient without fault, not skilled in martial arts, fond of guests and banquets; dwelling at home commanding the multitude—all obtained his joyful hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Youming was mild, unwarlike, and hospitable, beloved at home.

sentences.zh: 以子儀勛業，累歷大卿監，大歷八年卒，贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: Because of Ziyi's merit and enterprise, he successively held grand minister and supervisor posts; died in the eighth year of Dali; posthumously granted Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Through Ziyi's merit he rose to high office; died in Dali 8, posthumously grand mentor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 子昕，肅宗末為四鎮留後。

translations.literal: Son Xin, at the end of Suzong's reign was regent of the Four Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xin was Four Garrisons regent under Suzong.

sentences.zh: 自關、隴陷蕃，為虜所隔，其四鎮、北庭使額，李嗣業、荔非元禮皆遙領之。

translations.literal: Since Guan and Long fell to Tibet and were cut off by the barbarians, the Four Garrisons and Beiting commissioner titles—Li Siye and Lifei Yuanli—were both held remotely.
translations.idiomatic: After Tong and Long fell, Li Siye and Lifei Yuanli held Four Garrisons and Beiting titles in name only.

sentences.zh: 昕阻隔十五年，建中二年，與伊西北庭節度使李元忠俱遣使於朝，德宗嘉之。

translations.literal: Xin was cut off fifteen years; in the second year of Jianzhong, with Yixi-Beiting military commissioner Li Yuanzhong both sent envoys to court; Dezong praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off fifteen years, in Jianzhong 2 Xin and Li Yuanzhong sent envoys to court; Dezong praised them.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「四鎮、二庭，統任西夏五十七蕃十姓部落，國朝以來，相次率職。

translations.literal: The edict said: "The Four Garrisons and Two Courts overall charge the Western Xia's fifty-seven barbarian tribes and ten surnames' clans; since our dynasty, they successively led duty.
translations.idiomatic: The edict recalled the Four Garrisons and Beiting governing western tribes since the dynasty's rise.

sentences.zh: 自關、隴失守，東西阻絕，忠義之徒，泣血相守，慎固封略，奉尊朝法，皆候伯守將交修共理之所致也。

translations.literal: Since Guan and Long were lost, east and west blocked and cut off, the loyal and righteous, weeping blood, guarded each other, carefully solidifying borders, revering court law—all from marquises, guards, and generals jointly cultivating shared governance.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal garrisons held the frontier by joint effort though cut off from the east.

sentences.zh: 伊西北庭節度使李元忠，可北庭大都護；

translations.literal: Yixi-Beiting military commissioner Li Yuanzhong may be Beiting Grand Protector;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanzhong was named Beiting grand protector;

sentences.zh: 四鎮節度留後郭昕，可安西大都護、四鎮節度使。

translations.literal: Four Garrisons regent Guo Xin may be Anxi Grand Protector, Four Garrisons military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was named Anxi grand protector and Four Garrisons commissioner.

sentences.zh: 其將吏已下敘官，可超七資。」

translations.literal: For officers and clerks below, narrating office may skip seven ranks."
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates could advance seven ranks.

sentences.zh: 李元忠，本姓曹，名令忠，以功賜姓名。

translations.literal: Li Yuanzhong originally surnamed Cao, named Lingzhong; because of merit was granted the surname and name.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanzhong was born Cao Lingzhong and received his new name for merit.

sentences.zh: 時昕使自回紇歷諸蕃部，方達於朝。

translations.literal: At that time Envoy Xin came through Uyghurs and various barbarian departments before reaching court.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's envoys passed through Uyghurs and many tribes to reach court.

sentences.zh: 又有袁光庭者，為伊州刺史，隴右諸郡皆陷，光庭堅守伊州，吐蕃攻之累年，兵盡食竭，光庭先刃其妻子，自焚而死。

translations.literal: Also there was Yuan Guangting, Yizhou prefect; all Longyou commanderies fell; Guangting firmly held Yizhou; Tibet attacked for years until troops exhausted and food gone; Guangting first blade-killed his wife and children and self-immolated in fire.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou prefect Yuan Guangting held for years, then killed his family and burned himself when Tibet exhausted him.

sentences.zh: 因昕使知之，贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: Through Envoy Xin this was learned; posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Learning via Xin's envoy, the court posthumously made Yuan minister of works.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：天寶之季，盜起幽陵，萬乘播遷，兩都覆沒。

translations.literal: The historian said: In the Tianbao era's season, bandits rose in Youling; the myriad chariot was driven about; both capitals were overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: The historian wrote: In Tianbao's fall rebels rose and both capitals fell.

sentences.zh: 天祚土德，實生汾陽。

translations.literal: Heaven's fortune was the virtue of earth—it truly bore Fenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's earth virtue bore Guo of Fenyang.

sentences.zh: 自河朔班師，關西殄寇，身扞豺虎，手披荊榛。

translations.literal: From Hebei armies withdrawn, Guanxi exterminated bandits—body blocking wolves and tigers, hand parting thorns and brambles.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew from Hebei, cleared Guanxi, and fought through thorns and wolves.

sentences.zh: 七八年間，其勤至矣，再造王室，勛高一代。

translations.literal: Within seven or eight years his toil reached the utmost—again creating the royal house, merit high for one generation.
translations.idiomatic: In seven or eight years of toil he remade the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 及國威復振，群小肆讒，位重懇辭，失寵無怨。

translations.literal: When national prestige revived, petty men unrestrained in slander; rank heavy yet earnestly declining, losing favor without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm revived, slander grew; he declined high rank without bitterness.

sentences.zh: 不幸危而邀君父，不挾憾以報仇讎，晏然效忠，有死無二，誠大雅君子，社稷純臣。

translations.literal: Not fortunately in danger to hold the lord and father hostage, not bearing grudges to repay enemies; peacefully effecting loyalty, having death without duality—truly a great elegant gentleman, a pure minister of the altars.
translations.idiomatic: He never held the emperor hostage or nursed revenge; loyal unto death—a pure pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 自秦、漢已還，勛力之盛，無與倫比。

translations.literal: Since Qin and Han, the splendor of merit and strength—none comparable.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qin and Han none matched his merit.

sentences.zh: 而晞、曖於缞粗之中，拔身虎口，赴難奉天，可謂忠孝之門有嗣矣。

translations.literal: Yet Xi and Ai, in coarse hemp mourning, pulled themselves from the tiger's mouth, went to difficulty at Fengtian—one may say the gate of loyalty and filial piety had heirs.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and Ai, in mourning, escaped Zhu Ci and reached Fengtian—loyalty ran in the family.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：猗歟汾陽，功扶昊蒼。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Grand is Fenyang, merit upholding the azure heavens.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium sings: Great Fenyang, upholding heaven.

sentences.zh: 秉仁蹈義，鐵心石腸。

translations.literal: Upholding benevolence treading righteousness, iron heart and stone guts.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence and righteousness, heart of iron.

sentences.zh: 四朝靜亂，五福其昌。

translations.literal: Four reigns pacifying chaos, five blessings flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Four reigns, five blessings.

sentences.zh: 為臣之節，敢告忠良。

translations.literal: As minister's integrity—dare tell the loyal and good.
translations.idiomatic: His example speaks to all loyal ministers.
